articles.title: Hearing in SEC's lawsuit vs. LSU, Lane Kiffin delayed, conference no longer expected to discuss kicking Tigers out
articles.summary: The conference filed its suit ahead of Week 1 as LSU flirted with the idea of signing two players who were on NFL training camp rosters.
articles.body:
Tensions appear to be cooling between the SEC and LSU .

Wednesday's scheduled court hearing regarding the conference's lawsuit against the school and coach Lane Kiffin was continued to a later date. The continuance comes a day after LSU filled its final two open roster spots and will not be able to roster TE Dae'Quan Wright and DT Zxavian Harris during the 2026 season.

Sources told Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger that the decision to delay the hearing came after calls between LSU president Wade Rousse and SEC commissioner Greg Sankey.

A Thursday meeting of SEC schools is still scheduled , though sources told Dellenger that expulsion of LSU from the conference is no longer set to be discussed.

Harris and Wright were on NFL training camp rosters this summer and had committed to play for LSU following a Louisiana ruling that gave them a fifth year of eligibility. The two players were part of the 2022 recruiting class and among a group of players who had played four seasons in four years and unable to benefit from the NCAA's new five-in-five rule announced in June.

As LSU and Kiffin moved to potentially add Wright and Harris, two former Ole Miss players, for this season, the SEC announced that players who had signed NFL contracts were barred from playing in the conference. The two players were also in violation of the league's rule banning intraconference transfers from outside the transfer portal. Since they were plaintiffs in the Louisiana case, they were given a week after the ruling to transfer to a new school.

The SEC's suit was filed ahead of Week 1 and before LSU had submitted its 2026 roster. The Tigers did so on Friday, and had 103 of their 105 scholarship spots filled. While Harris and Wright were not on the roster ahead of LSU's blowout win over Clemson, they could have been added at some point in the season.

However, now that the spots have been filled, there's no pathway for them to play for the team in 2026. Rousse even said as much in a letter to the SEC himself.

After LSU filled the roster spots Tuesday night, the attorney for Wright and Harris told Dellenger that the players were reviewing their legal options. LSU's basketball team also has a commitment from former St. John's guard RJ Luis, who has appeared in three preseason NBA games.

articles.title: Ødegaard derriba el muro napolitano
articles.standfirst: El Arsenal impuso su dominio y se llevó los tres puntos ante el Nápoles
articles.summary: El Arsenal impuso su dominio y se llevó los tres puntos ante el Nápoles
articles.body: La Champions volvía a rugir en el Diego Armando Maradona con dos equipos dispuestos a escribir un nuevo capítulo en su historia europea. El Arsenal, finalista y con pleno de victorias en la fase de grupos el pasado curso, iniciaba otro intento de conquistar una ‘Orejona’ que todavía se le resiste. El Nápoles, obligado a pasar página después de un curso continental para olvidar, buscaba recuperar su mejor versión ante su público tras dos derrotas ligueras seguidas. Lo hacía, además, sin una de sus piezas importantes, McTominay, ausente tras someterse a una operación de corazón. Eso sí, regresaba De Bruyne al once. El conjunto de Arteta terminó imponiendo su ley y se llevó la victoria gracias a un golazo de Ødegaard. Ambos equipos buscaban ser dueños de la pelota desde el comienzo, aunque con el paso de los minutos fueron los 'gunners' quienes impusieron su dominio. Se acercaban con relativa facilidad al área acumulando hombres , aunque su ataque pecaba de estático. Saka probó una tijera en el 12' que atrapó Meret y, dos minutos después, De Bruyne obligó a intervenir a Raya con un disparo desde la frontal. La ocasión más clara del primer acto llegó en el 22', cuando Merino remató de cabeza en el corazón del área tras una gran dejada de Eze, encontrándose con un paradón de Meret. El conjunto inglés siguió llevando el peso del encuentro en el tramo final, pero no conseguía convertir su dominio en ocasiones claras. Y las que tenía, las mandaba por arriba de la portería. El Nápoles, esperaba a la contra, con varios disparos flojos que atrapó Raya. Saka tuvo la oportunidad más peligrosa antes del descanso, aunque su remate se marchó por encima del larguero. Raro para un jugador de su talla. El segundo tiempo arrancó con novedad bajo palos en el Nápoles. Milinković-Savić sustituyó a Meret, que no pudo continuar por problemas físicos. En el 49’, Hincapié tuvo otra buena oportunidad, pero su remate se marchó, otra vez, por encima del larguero. El guion apenas cambió tras el descanso, con un monólogo del conjunto londinense y un Nápoles cada vez más hundido en su propio campo, que resistían como podían. El Arsenal llegaba una y otra vez, no conseguían resolver. Al 70', ya acumulaba 20 remates. Arteta buscó agitar el encuentro desde el banquillo y recurrió a dos de sus fichajes, Guimarães y Tzolis. Tanto insistió el Arsenal que en el 75’ terminó derribando el muro. Ødegaard apareció para inventarse un auténtico golazo, un disparo imposible para Milinković-Savić. El combinado de Allegri, obligado a reaccionar, dejó más espacios y el Arsenal pudo sentenciar. En el 84’, Madueke y Tzolis protagonizaron una doble ocasión clarísima que no terminó en el segundo. En el 88’, llegó la única del conjunto local. De Bruyne tuvo una buena oportunidad para poner el empate, pero optó por buscar el pase en lugar del disparo y no encontró a ningún compañero dentro del área. El Arsenal, con un partido muy trabajado, se lleva los primeros tres puntos y presenta su candidatura para la Champions.

articles.title: El Chelsea de Xabi remonta un 0-2 con ¡seis goles en menos de media hora!
articles.standfirst: Increíble clasificación de los 'blues' para la siguiente ronda de la Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Increíble clasificación de los 'blues' para la siguiente ronda de la Carabao Cup
articles.body: El Chelsea de Xabi Alonso consiguió una increíble clasificación para la siguiente ronda de la Carabao Cup después de una alucinante remontada ante el Leeds United, que llegó a ponerse 0-2 en el marcador en el minuto 48, ya en la segunda parte. Pero entonces empezó la máquina Blue del técnico vasco que en menos de media hora, del minuto 53 al minuto 80, consiguió seis goles que pusieron un marcador final de 6-3 para los locales ante el delirio de un abarrotado Stamford Bridge. La remontada la inició Cole Palmer, que fue suplente y salió en el descanso para solucionar el partido. Dos goles suyos, en apenas dos minutos, pusieron el 2-2 en el marcador allá por el minuto 55. A partir de ahí, vino otra catarata de goles para los locales, que marcaron por obra de Neto, un doblete de Welbeck y un último tanto del argentino Valentín Barco para el 6-3 final en el minuto 80. La clasificación del Chelsea se había iniciado con un once inicial de Xabi con algunos suplentes, como el español Pep Chavarría, que sí fue fundamental en la remontara pues jugó los 90 minutos, aunque no dio ninguna asistencia. La salida en el minuto 45 de Reese James, Morgan Rogers, el citado Cole Palmer y Pedro Neto hicieron una revolución en el once londinense que acabó con un 6-3 que representa uno de los marcadores más impresionantes de lo que llevamos de la temporada dentro de los principales campeonatos de Europa.

images.caption: Xabi, con el Chelsea.

articles.title: Norwich 2-1 Birmingham: Philippe Clement's side secure third win in four games after win at Carrow Road
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Norwich and Birmingham at Carrow Road; Oscar Schwartau opened the scoring before Papa Diallo added a second; Carlos Vicente pulled one back but the hosts held on to win
articles.body:
First-half goals from Oscar Schwartau - with a real screamer - and Papa Diallo - his first for the club - saw off a strong challenge from Blues, for whom a second-half effort from Carlos Vicente was scant consolation.

The Spaniard wasted a glorious chance to equalise near the end as Chris Davies' men slipped to their first league defeat of the season in a game they should have taken something from on the balance of play.

Birmingham had the better of the early exchanges at Carrow Road and thought they had taken the lead in the 22nd minute when Liam Miller popped up at the back post to convert.

But their joy was cut short by the assistant's flag going up for offside, with replays showing it was an extremely tight decision.

Jay Stansfield had earlier brought a good reaction save out of Vladan Kovacevic after being played in by Miller, but it was Norwich who took the lead in the 28th minute with a real cracker of a goal.

There seemed little danger when Schwartau picked up the ball in a central area but the young Dane had other ideas, advancing to the edge of the D before lashing an unstoppable right-footed drive past James Beadle.

It was the Canaries' first effort of note of the game - and they made their second count as well to double their advantage in the 39th minute.

This time Andre Brooks got to the right byline and had time to look up and pick out and unmarked Diallo to sidefoot home the simplest of goals.

Birmingham missed a decent chance to pull one back just before the break when Miller fired just over after good work by Stansfield, leaving Norwich in command of a match which had seen them on the back foot for much of the half.

After a scrappy start to the second period Birmingham got themselves back in the game after 64 minutes with a well-worked goal. Millar was the architect, working himself some space on the left before squaring for Vicente to slide home from just outside the six-yard box.

With 20 minutes remaining, Norwich welcomed striker Jovon Makama back after seven months on the sidelines but it was midfielder Pelle Mattsson who almost restored their two-goal advantage with a low shot which brought a brilliant save out of Beadle.

Vicente wasted a glorious chance to level five minutes from time after being handed a clear sight of goal by Stansfield before Beadle foiled Anthony Musaba at point-blank range.

"We were up against a team who are very direct, a team who have won the most headed duels in the Championship this season, so it was important that we stepped up to the challenge.

"I am delighted to say that all the players did that. I think the fans could see they were giving everything out there to get the result we all wanted.

"At times we were able to play our football but we had to win our battles too. It is a really important step in the journey we are taking with this club.

"It is not the sort of football I like to see too much but I am delighted with the result. We have a really good group of players here, I love them all, and I feel they can do something special."

"In my 118 games in charge I can't remember feeling so disappointed with the officials as I am tonight. So many decisions went against us.

"We started really well and scored a goal from an onside position so I have been told.

"I hate VAR re-refereeing games for fouls because that is subjective, but offside is objective, you are either on or off, and I think it should be used in this league for incidents like that.

"Having said that we have to take responsibility for the next 15 minutes when we were far too open and conceded two goals that were far too easy for them.

"In the end that gave us too much to do but outside that spell we kept on going, got a deserved goal and might have got an equaliser at the end but unfortunately it wasn't to be."

articles.title: Prince William joins Kane and Shearer in campaign to prevent suicide through sport
articles.summary: The prince's new project aims to use the reach of sport to raise awareness about suicide and to show people the help available in a crisis.
articles.body:
The Prince of Wales is launching a scheme that aims to use the influence of sport to help prevent suicides, with the support of sports stars including Harry Kane, Kelly Holmes and Alan Shearer.

"Sport has the ability to reach people who may never walk through the door of a mental healthcare service," Prince William is expected to say at an event at Everton's football ground on Thursday.

"People who may never seek support themselves and may be struggling in silence," the prince will say later.

The On Your Side project wants to give people confidence to start the "difficult conversations" with friends, relations, teammates or colleagues who might be struggling with their mental health.

It aims to use the reach of sport to raise awareness about suicide and to show people the help available in a crisis, with the Football Association, Premier League and Team GB providing support.

Thursday's event will be Prince William's biggest public appearance in the UK since the return of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex.

Earlier this week, he attended the funeral of Norway's King Harald in Oslo and brought his son Prince George to his first day as a boarder at Eton College.

The level of suicide is disproportionately higher among men than women - it's the biggest cause of death for men under the age of 50 in the UK.

"My hope is that every sporting organisation in the country will look at what is being launched today and ask a question: 'What more can we do?' Because the opportunity before us is enormous," Prince William will say.

A film has been made, featuring England football captain Harry Kane and boxer Carl Frampton, talking about the importance of stepping in and offering help if people see someone who seems to be facing mental health problems.

Prince William helps to narrate the video, which aims to tackle the stigma around mental health and suicide, with 7,000 lives being lost to suicide each year in the UK.

The initiative has a practical toolkit, on a free website, for people who are worried or embarrassed about what to say to someone if they have concerns about their wellbeing.

It offers a sports-themed way of approaching the topic, called GOALS, representing G: get ready; O: open the conversation; A: ask the question; L: listen and respond and S: support and signpost.

Alan Shearer, former England football star and TV pundit, described it as "the first suicide prevention toolkit designed for the whole of UK sport".

"You don't have to be an expert. You don't have to have all the answers," said Shearer. "But we can all be better at asking, listening, and helping someone find the right support."

Shearer said it was particularly poignant that the launch would be at Everton, one of the clubs where Gary Speed had played, a friend of Shearer's who died by suicide in 2011.

The project has been created with mental health charities, including Chasing the Stigma, which has an app called Hub of Hope which claims to have the UK's largest mental health directory of places to get help.

The charity's founder Jake Mills said he had faced his own mental health challenges and saw sport as an effective route for this type of message.

He said sport was a "real force for good" in bringing people together and for "looking out for one another".

Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said he wanted to see sports organisations "creating a culture where conversations about well-being are really encouraged. Where people feel comfortable asking for help and also know where to get it".

Backing the project on Thursday in Liverpool will be former athlete Kelly Holmes, commentator Gabby Logan and former England footballer Jill Scott.

Prince William has been a longstanding campaigner over mental health and preventing suicide, with his Royal Foundation having last year launched the National Suicide Prevention Network.

articles.title: World Suicide Prevention Day: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit On Your Side
articles.summary: Prince William urges sport at every level to make suicide prevention part of its culture through a new nationwide toolkit called On Your Side.
articles.body:
Prince William has urged sport at every level to make suicide prevention part of its culture through a new nationwide toolkit.

Launched by the Prince of Wales and the Royal Foundation, On Your Side , external is a set of resources available online that aims "to make suicide prevention as much a part of sport as warm-up, training and performance".

The project is backed by more than 70 organisations including the Football Association, Premier League, Team GB, British Cycling and a host of leading mental health charities.

"Through my work on mental health, I have met people whose lives have been changed forever by suicide," said Prince William. "But I have also met people whose lives have been saved because someone stepped in to help."

The 44-year-old Royal, who has previously spoken about his own struggles with mental health issues, said that while he acknowledges the good work being done by current services, too often "initiatives are fragmented" and "support is inconsistent, particularly at a grassroots level".

William added that he hopes On Your Side provides everyone involved in sport who notices someone is struggling the "clear, practical guidance" to help that person find the support they need.

On Your Side is being launched to coincide with World Suicide Prevention Day on 10 September.

William says it has taken 'long time to understand my emotions'

According to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), there were 6,190 suicides registered in England and Wales in 2024.

It remains the biggest cause of death for men under the age of 50 and the rate remains notably higher among males (17.6 per 100,000 people) than females (5.7 per 100,000).

A promotional video for On Your Side features England men's football captain Harry Kane, F1 driver George Russell and Women's Rugby World Cup winner Rochelle 'Rocky' Clark.

The toolkit will officially be launched at Everton 's Hill Dickinson Stadium, a venue chosen because its construction included a 'talking bench' in memory of former player Gary Speed.

Ex-Wales captain and manager Speed, who also played for Leeds , Bolton, Newcastle and Sheffield United, took his own life in November 2011.

Premier League record goalscorer and Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer, who was a close friend of Speed, is among the athletes to have given their backing to the initiative.

"For me, this is obviously very personal," said Shearer.

"We can't always know when somebody is struggling, but we can all be better at asking, listening, and helping someone find the right support.

"You don't have to be an expert. You don't have to have all the answers, but I hope that everyone in sport will use the toolkit."

Prince William said he wants On Your Side to take advantage of sport's "remarkable ability to bring people together".

He added: "In moments of need, the right support can make all the difference. We all have the power to help, and that's why suicide prevention must be an important part of everyday sporting life."

The National Health Service, the Samaritans and mental health charity Mind were all consulted during the creation of On Your Side.

The Royal Foundation said the project had taken two years to complete and added that, although it was being launched to coincide with World Suicide Prevention Day, the initiative is "not a one-day campaign" and hopes it will have a long-lasting legacy.

If you, or someone you know, has been affected by any of the issues in this article, then support and information is available at BBC Action Line.

articles.title: The potential replacement for Dabo Swinney at Clemson is staring the Tigers right in the face
articles.summary: Tony Elliott's historic run at Virginia makes the Clemson Tigers alum and former coordinator the obvious choice if the Dabo Swinney era ends.
articles.body: If you've been paying attention at all, you know the Clemson Tigers are at a bit of a crossroads. Even casual college football fans can see the writing on the wall, as the once-proud national powerhouse has fallen on hard times, culminating in a 51-10 beatdown at the hands of LSU on Saturday night. I've written a lot about Tigers head coach Dabo Swinney and the thin line between respecting his past accomplishments and ushering the program into the NIL era, but lately I've found myself wondering if he's used up his nine lives. HOW MUCH LONGER DOES CLEMSON HEAD COACH DABO SWINNEY REALISTICALLY HAVE IN DEATH VALLEY? Saturday wasn't anything new - Clemson getting clobbered by a quality opponent has happened quite often post-Covid – but the fact that the general public has changed its reaction to the ritualistic sacrifices from shock to apathy shows that the Tigers aren't what they used to be. And that starts at the top. It's probably not a hot take to say that it's time for Clemson to make a change at head coach. The game appears to be passing Dabo by at warp speed, and although he won the ACC and made the College Football Playoff just two seasons ago, the conference is only getting tougher, and opponents like Miam, which used to be stepping stones for the Tigers on their way to a championship, are now leaning into the "new model" and lapping the old rulers of the realm. But getting rid of a coach is only half of the equation, and the question still remains: Who does Clemson replace Swinney with should it choose to move on from him? The Tigers are one of the few "haves" in a world of "have nots," meaning they could pick from a list of elite head coaches and not have to go too far down before hearing a "yes." However, going "big game hunting" isn't always the answer. Texas A&M, LSU, and USC are all some of the biggest brands in college football, and when they were in the market for a head coach, all three went after names who were "too big to fail." The Aggies secured Jimbo Fisher, who had won a national championship at Florida State less than half a decade ago. The Tigers and Trojans were searching for a new head coach during the same hiring cycle, and both came away with options that were deemed absolute coups at the time in Brian Kelly and Lincoln Riley, respectively. Today, only one of those three coaches is still employed by the last school to hire him, as Fisher and Kelly both failed to live up to the lofty expectations placed upon them when they arrived on campus. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Riley is still plugging away at USC, and although things seem to be trending up in Los Angeles, he's in year five without a single Playoff appearance to show so far, hardly the type of tenure any Trojans fan would have envisioned when they plucked him from Oklahoma in late 2021. All that is to say, Clemson doesn't need to hire the "sexy name" to have a successful coaching search. They need to hire the right guy. And I believe the answer is staring the Tigers right in the face. If Clemson pulls the plug on the Dabo Swinney era, its first call should be to Tony Elliott at Virginia. Elliott is fairly young for a head coach at only 46 years old, and he has the Cavaliers trending in a historic direction. After increasing Virginia's conference win totals every season since arriving in Charlottesville, Elliott guided the Cavs to an 11-win season and an ACC title game berth. Those 11 wins were the most in school history, and the up-and-coming head coach was awarded the Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year award for his efforts. He has the Cavaliers ranked in the AP Top-25 again this season after a rout of NC State in week zero, a team many thought would be a darkhorse contender in the ACC. It doesn't take a rocket scientist to see that Clemson has far more resources and deeper pockets for football than Virginia. If he's doing this well with the Cavaliers in the same conference, imagine what Elliott could do with the Tigers. But it's not just his coaching acumen that should have him at the top of the list. Because Tony Elliott is also a Clemson alum. He played for the Tigers in the early 2000s, and in addition to that, he was the offensive coordinator under Swinney for seven seasons, helping his alma mater win two national championships in the process. The idea of having an alum coach his school is becoming increasingly popular, particularly in the ACC. Brent Key (Georgia Tech), Jeff Brohm (Louisville), and Mario Cristobal (Miami) are all coaching at the schools they played for, and experiencing great success in the process. Elliot is crushing the previous baseline established at Virginia, he will be a hot name in any coaching search for the next few seasons, and he's a former player and coordinator with the Tigers. Let's not overthink this, Clemson. Dabo's replacement is there for the taking, just make the call.

articles.title: Today in sports history, October 27
articles.summary: Today in sports history, October 27
articles.body:
1906 : Massillon quarterback George "Peggy" Parratt completed a pass to Dan "Bullet" Riley in a victory over a combined Benwood-Moundsville team, recording the first authenticated forward-pass completion in professional football history.

1963 : Detroit Red Wings legend Gordie Howe scored his 544th career NHL regular-season goal, tying Maurice Richard's all-time league record.

1974 : France's Chantal Langlacé set a women's marathon world record of 2:46:24 in Neuf-Brisach, France.

1984 : Washington State running back Rueben Mayes rushed for 357 yards against Oregon, setting an NCAA single-game rushing record at the time.

1984 : Hakeem Olajuwon, then known as Akeem Olajuwon, made his NBA debut and helped the Houston Rockets defeat the Dallas Mavericks.

1985 : Bret Saberhagen pitched a five-hit shutout as the Kansas City Royals routed the St. Louis Cardinals 11-0 in Game 7 to win the first World Series championship in franchise history.

1985 : Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Anthony Carter began a streak of 105 consecutive NFL games with at least one reception.

1986 : The New York Mets overcame an early three-run deficit and defeated the Boston Red Sox 8-5 in Game 7 to win their second World Series championship.

1991 : Jack Morris pitched a 10-inning shutout and Gene Larkin delivered a walk-off single as the Minnesota Twins defeated the Atlanta Braves 1-0 in Game 7 of the World Series.

1992 : The Houston Rockets defeated the Dallas Mavericks 104-102 in a preseason game in Mexico City, the first NBA game played in Latin America.

1999 : The New York Yankees defeated the Atlanta Braves 4-1 to complete a World Series sweep, win their 25th championship and close the century with a record-tying 12th consecutive World Series victory. Mariano Rivera was named series MVP.

articles.title: SEC Not Expected to Vote on LSU's Membership This Week, AP Source Says
articles.summary: NEW ORLEANS (AP) — The Southeastern Conference is no longer expected to vote on whether to expel LSU from the league on Thursday, a person familiar with the matter said Wednesday evening.
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS (AP) — The Southeastern Conference is no longer expected to vote on whether to expel LSU from the league on Thursday, a person familiar with the matter said Wednesday evening.

The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because Thursday's meeting — to be held by video conference — is not open to the public and because the SEC has not released a statement on the matter since a federal court filing on Tuesday highlighted the league's intent to vote on LSU's membership.

The dispute between the conference and LSU stems largely from first-year Tigers coach Lane Kiffin's now-abandoned bid to field two players who had signed NFL contracts as undrafted rookies this past offseason.

New report on ex-pros joining LSU's roster

Report Card Grades for CFB's Top QBs 🧑‍🏫

A hearing scheduled Wednesday in a federal lawsuit the SEC filed against LSU was postponed by a judge in Birmingham, Alabama.

Meanwhile, LSU President Wade Rousse sent a one-page letter, obtained by the AP, to SEC commissioner Greg Sankey stating that the league's claims in its lawsuit against LSU are now moot because Kiffin had complied with a conference ban on rostering players who had previously signed contracts with NFL teams.

Rousse noted that he called Sankey last Friday afternoon and notified him personally that LSU would not be placing tight end Dae'Quan Wright or defensive tackle Zxavian Harris on the Tigers' roster.

Wright had spent part of the past offseason with the Philadelphia Eagles and Cleveland Browns. Harris has spent part of the offseason with the New Orleans Saints. Both also had played for Mississippi when Kiffin was the Rebels' coach.

LSU on Tuesday filled remaining vacancies on its roster with eligible players.

"The roster is now locked for the season," Rousse's letter stated. "LSU complied with SEC rules. This issue is moot."

Rousse also noted that LSU "will not challenge, disrupt or seek to cancel or postpone" Thursday's scheduled meeting — a concern Sankey had raised Tuesday in the SEC's amended federal complaint against LSU.

LSU is a founding member of the SEC, which was formed in 1933. LSU has a host of powerhouse athletics programs and has won three of the SEC's 25 AP national championships in football alone.

Still, the language in the federal lawsuit left little ambiguity about the extent to which the leaders of most SEC universities had become frustrated with LSU — not only because of efforts to recruit former pros to both its football and men's basketball teams.

They also were unhappy about the related court drama that ensued — including a marathon court hearing last week in which Sankey took the stand to insist the league has the right to enforce its own rules.

Sankey said there was consensus among conference leaders that "LSU's continued membership in the conference would be inconsistent with the publicly stated values and principles of the conference and its remaining member institutions," even if LSU doesn't put the former NFL players on its roster.

The SEC has a long-established rule forbidding teams from bringing players with major professional experience onto their rosters. In recent weeks, the conference announced updated enforcement provisions to that rule, stating that the commissioner had the power to suspend coaches, fine universities up to half of a sport's budget and restrict a member university's voting privileges on conference matters.

But last Thursday, a judge in Baton Rouge barred the league from enforcing any rules regarding former pros — a decision celebrated heartily by Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry and the state attorney general, Liz Murrill, who'd filed a brief in the case on behalf of the athletes.

Murrill called the SEC's lawsuit "legal garbage" shortly after it was filed last week.; The SEC has since listed Murrill as a defendant.

Sankey has stated that SEC presidents are concerned that Rousse and athletic director Verge Ausberry have no "meaningful control" over Kiffin or the football program.

Sankey also stated that "serious harm" had been caused "by the statements and conduct of LSU," and suggested that harm would not be undone simply by LSU renouncing "its intention to roster and play professional players on its football team."

Kiffin's hiring was one of two notable coaching changes at LSU involving the highest revenue-generating college sports: LSU also has brought back Will Wade to coach men's basketball. Wade was fired by previous athletic director Scott Woodward in the wake of an NCAA investigation into improper inducement payments to recruits when such payments were forbidden.

Wade served a suspension from coaching in college before returning in the 2023-24 season with McNeese State. He spent two seasons with the Cowboys and one with North Carolina State before he was brought back to LSU — a move favored by Landry, as well as Rousse, a Landry ally who was McNeese's president when Wade was there.

Wade has sought to sign RJ Luis Jr., a former Big East player of the year with St. John's who spent parts of the 2025 NBA offseason and preseason with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics, but never played in a regular-season NBA game.

Luis also has been fighting the NCAA in court in Baton Rouge, where a judge on Aug. 24 issued a preliminary injunction that temporarily blocks the NCAA from punishing LSU if the Tigers play Luis — something that also would violate the SEC rules at the center of the conference's federal lawsuit against LSU.

LSU's football team is now ranked eighth in the Top 25 AP Poll following Saturday's 51-10, season-opening victory over Clemson . The Tigers host Louisiana Tech on Saturday, followed by a much anticipated visit to No. 9 Ole Miss, where Kiffin will face the team he coached a year ago.

articles.summary: Football News: Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti has begun reshaping the national team after their disappointing 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign, naming a 26-man squad .
articles.body: Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti has begun reshaping the national team after their disappointing 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign, naming a 26-man squad for the upcoming friendlies against Australia and India.The squad includes some of Brazil's biggest names, with Real Madrid forward Vinícius Júnior, Barcelona winger Raphinha and Paris Saint-Germain veteran Marquinhos among the players selected by Ancelotti.Brazil will begin their post-World Cup schedule with two meetings against Australia. The first is scheduled for September 25 at Queensland Country Bank Stadium in Townsville, followed by another clash with the hosts on September 29 at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane.The five-time world champions will then travel to India for a historic fixture against the hosts on October 3. Brazil will face India for the first time in their history, with the match scheduled to begin at 7:30 PM IST at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata.Ancelotti begins Brazil overhaulAncelotti has made it clear that Brazil's next cycle will involve a significant reshaping of the squad, and his first selection since the World Cup reflects that approach.The Italian coach has included several young players, with a number of them also eligible to represent Brazil at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Ancelotti hopes the emerging group can eventually form the core of his side for the 2030 World Cup.The coach had indicated in an interview with The Associated Press in July, shortly after Brazil's World Cup exit, that he intended to look towards younger players as part of the team's rebuilding process."Coach Carlo Ancelotti called up a total of 26 players on Wednesday (9) for Brazil's first matches after the World Cup. Ten of them play in Brazilian football. He released the list at the headquarters of the Brazilian Football Confederation, in Rio, from where he then gave a press conference," the CBF said in a statement.The selection contains only a few of the players Ancelotti took to the World Cup three months ago, with the coach opting to introduce several fresh faces alongside established stars.Brazil looking to move on from World Cup disappointmentBrazil's World Cup campaign ended in the round of 16 after they suffered defeat to Norway in their pre-quarters clash.The result extended Brazil's wait for a sixth World Cup title. Their last triumph came in 2002, meaning the five-time champions have now gone without the trophy since their success in Japan and South Korea.Ancelotti's first assignment after that disappointment will therefore be to begin rebuilding a squad capable of challenging at the next World Cup.The upcoming Australia fixtures will provide his first opportunity to assess the new-look group before Brazil's historic meeting with India in Kolkata.Brazil squad for Australia, India friendliesGoalkeepers: Hugo Souza (Corinthians), Pedro Morisco (Coritiba), Otavio (Cruzeiro)Defenders: Arthur Dias (Athletico-PR), Douglas Santos (Zenit), Gabriel Magalhaes (Arsenal), Jair (Nottingham Forest), Marquinhos (PSG), Matheuzinho (Corinthians), Mauro Junior (PSV Eindhoven), Vitor Reis (Manchester City), Wesley (Rome)Midfielders: Andrey Santos (Manchester United), Breno Bidon (Corinthians), Bruno Guimarães (Arsenal), Danilo Santos (Botafogo), Douglas Luiz (Juventus), Gabriel Bontempo (Santos)Forwards: Endrick (Real Madrid), Stephen (Chelsea), John Peter (Chelsea), Pedro (Flamengo), Raphinha (Barcelona), Rayan (Bournemouth), Samuel Lino (Flamengo), Vinícius Júnior (Real Madrid)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mijatovic detecta los carencias del Madrid de Mourinho: "No hay que llorar"

articles.summary: "El Madrid puede mejorar, pero la gente está como revuelta y protestando. Y eso se mantendrá hasta que el equipo muestre algo diferente"
articles.body: Pedja Mijatovic, jugador del Real Madrid de 1996 a 1999 y director de fútbol de equipo blanco de 2006 a 2009, analizó en el programa 'El Larguero' el juego del equipo merengue y los pitos del Santiago Bernabéu a sus jugadores durante el partido de Champions que acabaron ganando 2-1. "Me sorprendieron porque íbamos ganando, pero vienen de dos años atrás. La gente ya viene enfadada por no ganar títulos estos años y les hace falta muy poquito para silbar. No están muy contentos", compartió en la SER. El exfutbolista de 57 años también apuntó que "el Madrid no deja garantías de que tiene equipo para ganar la Liga) y al "comportamiento de unos ciertos futbolistas que un momento determinado enfadan a la afición". "Es una falta de fútbol, pero los futbolistas tienes que seguir con su trabajo a pesar de tener a la gente en contra y Mourinho lo tiene bastante claro", destacó. Respecto al sello del Jose Mourinho en el actual Real Madrid compartió con Manu Carreño que "es pronto, pero se nota una cierta seriedad... Poco a poco Mou conseguirá lo que él quiere. Un equipo sólido, en bloque y que sea letal cuando pueda contragolpear". "Poco a poco. Hay que tener paciencia. No hay que juzgarles ahora por cinco partidos jugados", aconsejó. Pedja Mijatovic también habló sobre la falta de fútbol del Real Madrid de Mourinho y sobre si Bernardo Silva podría ser la solución a este problema del centro del campo merengue. "El Real Madrid tiene la capacidad de mejorar. No hay que llorar por los jugadores que ya no están y han hecho historia, como Luka Modric y Toni Kroos. Los echamos de menos... ¿pero dónde encontramos jugadores como estos dos? Hay que confiar en los que ya están y nunca compararlos con Modric y Toni Kroos", declaró el de Podgorica. Mijatovic destaca que "aún me falta un director de orquesta en el Real Madrid... que podría haber sido Rodri (fichajes estelar del Barcelona) sin ningún tipo de problemas, pero no ha podido ser y hay que buscarlo dentro de la plantilla". "El Madrid puede mejorar, pero la gente está como revuelta y protestando. Y eso se mantendrá hasta que el equipo muestre algo diferente", compartió.

articles.title: La nueva vida de Griezmann en la MLS con 35 años: doblete y 6 goles en 4 partidos
articles.standfirst: Antoine Griezmann (35 años) suma 6 goles en 4 partidos para poner a Orlando City en la lucha por los playoffs en la MLS
articles.summary: Antoine Griezmann (35 años) suma 6 goles en 4 partidos para poner a Orlando City en la lucha por los playoffs en la MLS
articles.body: El francés Antoine Griezmann firmó otro doblete en la MLS para lanzar a Orlando City en plena zona de 'playoffs', en una jornada entre semana en la que el uruguayo Bruno Damiani anotó un triplete en Philadelphia y en la que el duelo entre el Inter Miami de Leo Messi y Chicago Fire del polaco Robert Lewandowski acabó 1-1. Griezmann dio vida a Orlando con un doblete clave para la victoria 3-2 conseguida en el campo del Atlanta United del técnico argentino Gerardo Martino. El francés, exdelantero del Atlético de Madrid, lleva seis goles en los últimos cuatro partidos jugados con el equipo de Florida. En el Mercedes Benz Stadium, el galo igualó en el minuto 25 al rematar un centro raso de Joran Gerbet y, tras el 2-1 del colombiano Iván Angulo, selló su doblete al fulminar al meta en un mano a mano. Griezmann, de 35 años, anotó siete goles en sus primeros nueve partidos en la MLS. El Orlando, que antes de su llegada estaba fuera de los puestos de postemporada, ocupa ahora la sexta plaza en el Este, con 31 puntos. En el Soldier Field de Chicago, ante más de 63.000 espectadores, el Inter Miami y el Fire empataron 1-1 con goles de Lewandowski y del brasileño Casemiro. Lewandowski firmó el golazo del 1-1 con una volea a los 10 minutos y Casemiro empató de cabeza en el 48 tras un saque de esquina colgado por Leo Messi. Casemiro lleva tres goles con el Inter Miami, mientras que Lewandowski acumula siete con el Fire. El Inter Miami es segundo en el Este, con 44 puntos, cinco más que el Fire, cuarto. Entre los demás resultados, brilló en Philadelphia Bruno Damiani, que endosó un triplete al Cincinnati en el 5-0 de su equipo, en el que también se le anuló el posible póquer. Damiani había anotado tres goles en esta temporada e igualó esa marca este miércoles ante Cincinnati. El mexicano Daniel Ríos ilusionó al Montreal con un gol en la primera mitad, pero los canadienses fueron remontados por el Charlotte, mientras que el Toronto dio la sorpresa al remontar y tumbar al Nashville, dominador del Este de la MLS.

articles.title: Messi conecta a Casemiro, el rey de los cabezazos, para desactivar a Lewandowski en la MLS
articles.standfirst: Fue un partido entre exestrellas del Barcelona, con Messi y Luis Suárez en el Inter Miami, y Robert Lewandowski en Chicago Fire
articles.summary: Fue un partido entre exestrellas del Barcelona, con Messi y Luis Suárez en el Inter Miami, y Robert Lewandowski en Chicago Fire
articles.body: Leo Messi asistió y Casemiro anotó de cabeza su tercer gol consecutivo, pero el Inter Miami no pasó del 1-1 en su visita al Chicago Fire de Lewandowski en el estadio Soldier Field en la vigésima cuarta jornada de la MLS. El Soldier Field, que promedia cerca de 20.000 espectadores por partido, se llenó con más de 63.000 aficionados para ver a Messi en directo en la Ciudad del Viento. Fue un partido entre exestrellas del Barcelona, con Messi y el uruguayo Luis Suárez en el Inter Miami, y el polaco Robert Lewandowski, el estelar fichaje del Fire este verano. No faltó el gol de Lewandowski, que a los 10 minutos rompió al igualdad con una maravillosa volea tras un centro del lateral izquierdo Andrew Gutman. El polaco lleva siete goles en su nueva etapa en la MLS y anotó en sus últimos tres encuentros. La respuesta del Inter Miami llegó nada más arrancar la segunda mitad. Messi colgó un centro con la zurda desde saque de esquina y Casemiro firmó su tercer gol consecutivo de cabeza con la camiseta de las Garzas. Hubo polémicas en el Fire pues el último toque en la jugada que provocó el saque de esquina fue de Germán Berterame, según mostraron claramente las cámaras. El árbitro no lo vio y en el córner siguiente, Casemiro igualó el duelo. El Inter Miami, que sigue a la espera de la visa de trabajo de su nuevo entrenador Kily González, y que tuvo a Guillermo Hoyos en el banquillo en Chicago, empujó con fuerza, pero se topó con el monumental meta local Chris Brady. Para el Fire fue el cuarto empate consecutivo, mientras que el Inter Miami solo ganó uno de sus últimos siete partidos entre todas las competiciones No faltó intensidad en el Soldier Field y, en el tramo final, saltaron chispas entre Lewandowski y el argentino Rodrigo De Paul.

articles.title: Cañizares esclarece los motivos por los que "el Bernabéu castiga" a los jugadores del Madrid
articles.summary: Santiago Cañizares, que fue jugador del Real Madrid en dos etapas (1988 a 1992 y 1994 a 1998), analizó en el programa 'El Partidazo' de la Cadena COPE "lo que el Santiago Bernabéu" está castigando a sus jugadores.
articles.body: Santiago Cañizares, que fue jugador del Real Madrid en dos etapas (1988 a 1992 y 1994 a 1998), analizó en el programa 'El Partidazo' de la Cadena COPE "lo que el Santiago Bernabéu" está castigando a sus jugadores. "El Bernabéu no está castigando que los jugadores del Real Madrid sean mejores o peores. No se le puede discutir a Mbappé su capacidad goleadora o a otros jugadores su calidad táctica, pero lo que sí se les puede discutir es su implicación especialmente cuando no tienen el balón. Y yo creo que por ahí van los tiros", le explicó a Juanma Castaño el exfutbolista de 56 años. Cañizares subrayó que "el Bernabéu no castiga que falles uno o dos pases, al no ser que estés en una baja forma... El Bernabéu aprovecha cuando no estás del todo bien para recordarte que no estoy contento contigo con lo que estás haciendo sobre el terreno de juego y la implicación que tienes a diferencia con el resto de tus compañeros", expuso el de Puertollano.

articles.body: El programa 'El Partidazo de COPE' ha publicado un vídeo de la comentada reacción de Iker Casillas, embajador ICON de LALIGA, cuando le entregaron un cromo gigante de Jose Mourinho durante la presentación de los cromos oficiales de LaLiga de Panini. "No lo estoy viendo, pero tiene que ser super más intenso y super más trabajo. No sé quién será... ", contestó el exfutbolista entre risas. Recientemente Jose Mourinho habló sobre su relación con Iker Casillas cuando ambos coincidieron en el Real Madrid: "Me di cuenta de que estaban consentidos". Casillas recordó en el acto de presentación, en el que estuvieron Javier Tebas (presidente de LaLiga) y Juan Pedro Martínez (director editorial de Panini España), como pasó de coleccionar los cromos de sus ídolos a jugar con ellos: "Tú pasas de estar con ellos viéndolos en la tele a convivirlos en el día a día y en los entrenamientos, en el hotel, en los viajes, en los partidos, y, bueno, pues hace que ese sueño que tenía de pequeño de guardarlos en cromos y poder tenerlos en un álbum, incluso buscar algún día su firma, en mi caso, en la ciudad deportiva, en el hotel Real Madrid".

articles.title: El mejor doblaje de Europa
articles.standfirst: El Barça demuestra que tiene todas sus posiciones dobladas con jugadores de garantía
articles.summary: El Barça demuestra que tiene todas sus posiciones dobladas con jugadores de garantía
articles.body: Si algo quedó demostrado en el estreno europeo del Barça es que Hansi Flick cuenta con una plantilla sin parangón en Europa. Ante el Feyenoord, el técnico alemán tiró de rotación para demostrar que su equipo es de los pocos que tiene dobladas todas las posiciones. Los azulgrana este año tienen bien cubiertas las espaldas. En un año tan exigente donde se juega cada tres días y se afronta el difícil reto de intentar ganar todas las competiciones, las sanciones y lesiones en momentos puntuales suelen resultar decisivas para acometer ese ambicioso objetivo de levantar los grandes títulos a final de temporada. El Barça lo sabe y se ha preocupado esta temporada de mejorar su plantilla y tener un recambio de garantías en cada posición del campo. Eso le asegura repartir minutos, intentar minimizar el riesgo de lesiones por acumulación de partidos y que todos los jugadores lleguen en condiciones óptimas al momento decisivo del año. Solo basta con echar un vistazo a los minutos acumulados a estas alturas del curso en toda la plantilla para evidenciar esa gestión de recursos. Se fueron dos delanteros, Lewandowski y Ferran, pero ha llegado otro, Gabriel Jesús, y se ha reconvertido con éxito a Raphinha como referencia ofensiva. Ahí, de momento, no parece haberse debilitado el Barça. No se retuvo a Rashford pero en su lugar han llegado Anthony Gordon y Adeyemi. Aquí claramente es la posición en la que más ha ganado el Barça con respecto a temporadas pasadas. En mediocampo ha llegado Rodri y se ha ido Casadó y en defensa se ha repescado a Cancelo y la salida de Araujo se ha suplido con la consolidación de Espart en la primera plantilla. Flick ha reestructurado su primera línea y cuenta con varios jugadores capaces de jugar en diferentes posiciones, como el propio Cancelo, Eric García, Koundé o Gerard Martín. En portería, con Joan García como indiscutible, la salida definitiva de Ter Stegen se ha cubierto con la llegada de Livakovic, alternativa de mayor garantía que Szczesny, que pasa a partir de ahora a ser el tercer portero. Solo basta echar un ojo a las alineaciones de Flick para darse cuenta que puede permitirse refrescar la mayoría de las posiciones entre partido y partido. Únicamente Lamine, tras la lesión de Roony, se encuentra sin un recambio natural que le permita descansar con ciertas garantías. Ante el Feyenoord, descansaron Eric, Gerard Martín, Espart, Gordon y Fermín. Entraron Koundé, Christensen, Cancelo, Adeyemi y Olmo. Y el equipo no lo notó. Ese es el gran triunfo y el gran poder del Barça para esta temporada. Mientras Raphinha luce como nueve, además, Gabriel Jesús ya deja sus primeros destellos como recambio de lujo. Todo suena demasiado bien en un equipo que, seguramente, tenga el mejor doblaje de toda Europa. Y eso sin contar con Balde -relegado a tercer lateral izquierdo en el equipo- y Frenkie de Jong -lesionado para varios meses-. Y ahí puede estar la clave para el asalto definitivo a la Champions League.

articles.standfirst: Si se confirma la compra, el club estará sujeto desde ya a las decisiones del astro argentino
articles.summary: Si se confirma la compra, el club estará sujeto desde ya a las decisiones del astro argentino
articles.body: Lo primero que hay que decir del 'nuevo' Eldense de Leo Messi es que, legalmente, aún no se puede hablar de nueva propiedad, ya que el proceso de 'due diligence' (auditorías de compra) llevará un par de semanas antes de que la entidad cambie de propietario y sea considerado oficialmente el primer club profesional que tiene a Messi como máximo y único accionista al cien por cien. Pero, ¿por qué ha elegido Leo este modesto club de una pequeña localidad de Alicante llamada Elda de apenas 55.000 habitantes? La decisión de comprar el Eldense ha sido única y exclusiva del crack argentino, que conoce perfectamente al club y sus circunstancias. No han intervenido terceras personas ni otros cracks del fútbol como se ha rumoreado. El Eldense es un equipo pequeño, sí, pero con muchas posibilidades de crecimiento en el fútbol profesional. La idea de LM es, primero, mantener al equipo en Segunda división, cosa que no será fácil pues el equipo alicantino tiene actualmente dos puntos en las primeras cuatro jornadas, situación por la cual fue destituido el técnico Claudio Barragán el pasado lunes. Aún no hay nuevo entrenador. La primera decisión importante de Messi y su gente será ésa, nombrar nuevo entrenador, pues a pesar de que oficialmente no es aún su club, si espera tomar el control del mismo en estos días. Las decisiones de Leo llenarán todas las áreas de un club que tiene un estadio pequeño, el Nuevo Pepico Amat, en el centro de la ciudad, al igual que su Centro de entrenamiento. Un recinto con posibilidades también de crecer en los próximos años si todo se consolida. Desde que MARCA anunció esta posible compra, el Eldense y la ciudad de Elda han 'volado' en todos los medios del mundo y las redes sociales. Messi ha puesto a Elda en el foco del mundo, y así se lo agradeció el propio alcalde de la localidad este mismo miércoles. El dirigente de la ciudad, Rubén Alfaro, expresó su "satisfacción" y apeló al "respeto" por la confidencialidad del proceso, destacando el pacto preliminar por el que Lionel Messi compraría "en solitario" el Club Deportivo Eldense. Por supuesto, el astro argentino tiene pensado visitar la ciudad y el equipo en cuanto sus obligaciones con el Inter Miami se lo permitan, ya que, recordemos, la MLS se encuentra en plena competición y se alargará hasta principios de diciembre. Es ahí cuando se puede producir la visita de Leo... si no hay sorpresa antes, que nadie la descarta.

articles.summary: José Manuel Pinto, portero del F.C. Barcelona en la época de la 'guerra de los Clásicos' contra el Real Madrid de Mourinho ("Yo no agarré del cuello a Arbeloa, le di un cachetón"), le recuerda a Mou su legendario "¿por qué? que pasó a la historia en abril de 2011 después del partido de semifinales de la Champions entre Madrid y Barça.
articles.body: José Manuel Pinto, portero del F.C. Barcelona en la época de la 'guerra de los Clásicos' contra el Real Madrid de Mourinho ("Yo no agarré del cuello a Arbeloa, le di un cachetón"), le recuerda a Mou su legendario "¿por qué? que pasó a la historia en abril de 2011 después del partido de semifinales de la Champions entre Madrid y Barça. El exfutbolista de 50 años, que ahora triunfa como productor musical bajo el nombre de Wahin, ya se acordó de los "¿por qué? de Mourinho durante una celebraciones del Barça en 2011: "Si alguien se pregunta '¿por qué?' estamos aquí... ¿por qué?... ¡niños decírselo!: Porque somos los mejores...". Recientemente Pinto publicó un tema musical titulado "¿Por qué?", y lo ha recuperado después de las últimas nuevas de prensa de Mourinho en su segunda etapa en el Real Madrid. En la letra de la canción de Pinto se escucha "Tú te preguntas por qué... Porque soy mejor, bueno, ¿y qué?", "No te preguntes más por qué, por qué, por qué", "Yo a ti no te robé; jugando bien, te la quité" o "Te gané la liga de las estrellas".

articles.title: Corberán, al borde del mal que persigue a este Valencia: los 'reno-ceses' de entrenadores
articles.standfirst: El técnico amplió su contrato, de forma oficial, el pasado julio, con el anuncio del club hasta junio de 2028 en un ambiente ya de por sí enrarecido y que ahora es más tenso todavía
articles.summary: El técnico amplió su contrato, de forma oficial, el pasado julio, con el anuncio del club hasta junio de 2028 en un ambiente ya de por sí enrarecido y que ahora es más tenso todavía
articles.body: El Valencia de Meriton es volátil. Sobre todo con decisiones que se van tomando -renovaciones de entrenadores- y que a los pocos meses éstas quedan retratadas -destituciones- dando pie a una gestión extraña. Es el caso de uno de los elementos más importantes en un club de fútbol. La figura del entrenador que al fin y a la postre es el que debe ofrecer el primer signo de estabilidad deportiva para que todo funcione. Pero en el Valencia el papel de entrenador es una figura compleja. En exceso. No hay más que ver el capítulo de renovaciones de entrenadores y lo que ha ocurrido después. Porque no es uno ni dos... el Valencia se ha convertido en una tendencia difícil de asumir porque se han tenido que pagar indemnizaciones millonarias que, evidentemente, han repercutido en el Fair Play Financiero con lo maltrecho que ya está este apartado. El primero que renovó su contrato fue Nuno Espirito Santo. Fue el primer técnico de la Era Meriton. Llegó en 2014 y antes de acabar logró una renovación por dos campañas. Lo que sucede es que el idilio con el entrenador portugués duró apenas unos meses. En noviembre de 2015 fue destituido tras una renovación pocos meses atrás. Otro caso, el de Pako Aiestarán. Llegó como complemento del cuerpo técnico de Gary Neville pero cuando éste fue destituido a finales de marzo de 2016 el vasco tomó las riendas. Acabó la temporada y el club decidió renovarle. Este nuevo 'enamoramiento' duró apenas cuatro jornadas de Liga. Cuatro derrotas y destitución. Otro 'finiquito' más a pagar tras una renovación. Esta historia sigue con Marcelino García Toral. Llegó en 2017 al Valencia y lo encumbró. Acabó renovando antes de acabar la temporada 2018-19, pero las desavenencias con la propiedad lo llevaron a un cese fulminante por parte de Peter Lim un 11de septiembre de 2019 después de las primeras tres jornadas. Otro pago de contrato cancelado anticipadamente. El siguiente en esta dinámica envolvente fue Rubén Baraja. Llegó en febrero de 2023 con una situación deportiva muy grave en puestos de descenso. Sacó al equipo de abajo. Había firmado por año y medio pero antes de acabar su contrato el club decidió renovarlo dos años más. En diciembre de 2024, varios meses después de anunciar su renovación, era destituido con el consiguiente pago de su contrato. Ahora llega la situación de Carlos Corberán que vive posiblemente el momento más delicado desde que es entrenador del Valencia. El técnico fue renovado oficialmente el pasado mes de julio. Hasta junio de 2028 pero el equipo da muestras de no funcionar con lo que se mira al banquillo ya... sobre todo tras lo visto en los últimos encuentros lo que provoca que haya un clima de tensión e incertidumbre en torno al preparador valenciano. Gourlay siempre lo ha defendido como el entrenador idóneo para este proyecto junto a la propiedad, pero la situación no es la misma que meses atrás.

articles.title: Odegaard looked smooth as silk in Naples
articles.summary: Martin Odegaard, as manager Mikel Arteta hinted, is almost playing like someone with something to prove.  Former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha said Od...
articles.body:
Martin Odegaard , as manager Mikel Arteta hinted, is almost playing like someone with something to prove.

He knows that while Arsenal had a season of glory last time out, his personal contribution was not what he expected from himself.

Former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha said Odegaard "will want to have a bigger impact on the team this season" on Match of the Day .

"They have got unfinished business in the Champions League," said Onuoha. "He wants to be the first captain of Arsenal to lift that trophy.

"You would not back against them winning it based on what we have seen them do in this competition in the past two seasons, but he 100% takes Arsenal to a different level when he is on form and playing like this.

"That's the way it should be as well. When he is at his best, Arsenal are at their best. The best version of Arsenal, in my opinion, comes when Odegaard is pulling the strings."

This time around, Odegaard looks smooth as silk - and it is no coincidence Arsenal look exactly the same.

"Arsenal have obviously looked good at the start of the season and he has been a big reason for that," added Onuoha. "Some of his creativity, especially on the right-hand side, has been excellent.

"He looks after the ball so well. He is always looking for that pass to be able to create opportunities. He even does defensive work as well."

Arsenal's superiority was illustrated by having 26 shots against Napoli , their most in a single Champions League match since records began in 2003-04.

The Champions League has proved elusive for Arsenal, with finals lost to Barcelona in 2006 and Paris St-Germain last season .

It remains their Holy Grail - but if Odegaard maintains his brilliant form, their chances of crossing a so far insurmountable barrier will increase hugely.

articles.title: El 'déjà vu' de Gabriel Jesus
articles.standfirst: El delantero brasileño marcó en su estreno en Champions ante el Feyenoord como hiciera en el Manchester City en 2017
articles.summary: El delantero brasileño marcó en su estreno en Champions ante el Feyenoord como hiciera en el Manchester City en 2017
articles.body: El estreno en Champions del Barcelona no pudo ser más redondo. Una nueva manita y todo un puñetazo en la mesa europea. Los de Flick van más en serio que nunca en esta edición. Al doblete de Raphinha, el estreno goleador de Lamine Yamal como capitán azulgrana y el golazo de Adeyemi se les unió Gabriel Jesus. El delantero puso la guinda en su debut en Champions como nuevo jugador del Barça. El ariete conoce muy bien esta competición. Es por eso que se movió como pez en el agua cuando salió al campo en el minuto 83' de partido y, en apenas dos minutos, logró abrir su cuenta personal con su nuevo escudo. Se dio la casualidad que repetía 'víctima'. Porque fue también ante el Feyenoord cuando se estrenó como goleador en Champions con la camiseta del Manchester City. Aquello sucedió en 2017 con Guardiola en el banquillo 'citizen'. Nueve años después, con Flick al mando y defendiendo el escudo del Barça, Gabriel Jesus volvía a marcar antes los de Róterdam. Casualidades de la vida y caprichos del destino. Para él, un déjà vu en toda regla. No sólo eso. El delantero se convirtió en el segundo jugador del Barça que menos tiempo ha necesitado marcar en su debut en Champions. El '9' anotó a los 2 minutos y 14 segundos, sólo superado por el gol que anotó Malcom en 2018 ante el Inter. El también brasileño marcó cuando llevaba apenas 1 minuto y 53 segundos en el césped.

articles.title: SDFC come up short at home, fall 3-2 to Earthquakes
articles.summary: San Diego FC’s Snapdragon Stadium winning streak snapped at five, downed 3-2 by in-state rivals, San Jose Earthquakes, on a warm Wednesday night.
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO --- San Diego FC 's Snapdragon Stadium winning streak snapped at five, downed 3-2 by in-state rivals, San Jose Earthquakes , on a warm Wednesday night.

SDFC were back home from their brief single-match Florida road trip, unable to collect points in their visit to Inter&Co Stadium, falling 1-0 to the Eastern Conference's Orlando City SC .

After falling 3-0 in their first meeting of the season back on April 4 at PayPal Park, SDFC looked to split the regular-season series on Wednesday night, in search of their sixth straight win at Snapdragon Stadium.

As for this match, the Earthquakes were quick to capitalize on the counter, getting on the scoresheet within three minutes of the opening whistle.

An all-SDFC start was flipped with a single pass, finding Earthquakes' midfielder Niko Tsakiris unmarked and with space in the attacking half. All that was left was a cutback onto his left foot as he left off a curling low shot from outside the box, into the bottom left side netting for the 1-0 score.

SDFC's nightmare start continued at the six-minute mark, with an Earthquake long ball turning into a defensive half turnover for SDFC, leaving CJ dos Santos forced to make a play on the ball with forward Preston Judd going down inside the box, quickly given as a penalty.

After an initial red card from referee Alexis Da Silva to CJ dos Santos following the foul on Judd, SDFC caught a break with the offence being downgraded to a yellow card as SDFC remained at 11 men on the field.

CJ dos Santos immediately came to SDFC's rescue, diving to his bottom left of the goal to deny Tsakiris from the spot in the eighth minute to keep the game at 1-0.

But the relentless counterattacks continued from San Jose, with Judd played in behind as he rounded CJ dos Santos and scored into the uncontested net for the 2-0 score in the 12-minute.

San Jose's Niko Tsakiris and Ousseni Bouda connected in the 35-minute to make it three goals in the first half, with Tsakiris delivering a distant outside-the-foot pass into the box for Bouda's well-timed lofted header over CJ dos Santos to make it 3-0.

Anders Dreyer gave SDFC a spark of life right before the halftime break, driving in a half-volleyed strike near the penalty spot off the left post and into the net.

The 3-1 score marked Dreyer's ninth goal of the 2026 MLS season.

CJ dos Santos wouldn't escape a red card for the second time in the game, receiving his second yellow of the match in the 80-minute after an outside-the-box challenge on Bouda.

Second-choice goalkeeper Duran Ferree was called upon to take over between the sticks for the remainder of the game.

Very late into the match, SDFC earned a penalty of their own in the 88-minute off a delivered Anders Dreyer set piece, ending in newly signed forward Cédric Bakambu being pushed from behind near the goal area by Earthquakes' Max Floriani , who saw his second yellow card of the game after a VAR review.

On his Chrome & Azul debut, Cédric Bakambu buried his attempt from the spot into the left side of the goal to record his first goal for the club, cutting the San Jose lead to a single score.

But time just ran out for the home side, with the full-time whistle blowing at that 3-2 scoreline for the San Jose Earthquakes' regular-season sweep, ending SDFC's five-match Snapdragon Stadium winning streak as the Chrome & Azul drop back-to-back MLS matches.

Following the match, SDFC head coach Mikey Varas addressed the team's recent struggles and performances at the postgame press conference.

"We played far away from our best. I just want to apologize to the fans, to Frontera and to everybody who follows the club because it's really not a good performance."

"We're at the business end of things where we need to give much stronger performances than that. That's 100% on me, I hold my hand up."

"I'm gonna do everything possible to help these guys, to set them up for success."

SDFC are back in action at the weekend, hosting Eastern Conference side Philadelphia Union on Sunday night as the two clubs meet for the first-ever time. Kickoff at Snapdragon Stadium is set for 6 p.m.

articles.title: 🥐 Barça up, Atleti down... 5️⃣ stories shaping Thursday
articles.summary: The Champions League opener leaves us with a brilliant start for FC Barcelona and a bitter setback for Atlético de Madrid. Off the pitch, Rodri puts his cont...
articles.body:
The Champions League opener leaves us with a brilliant start for FC Barcelona and a bitter setback for Atlético de Madrid . Off the pitch, Rodri puts his controversy with Valencia to bed, and Leo Messi brings Spanish football to a standstill with his imminent arrival as owner of CD Eldense.

A Barça five-star start to the Champions League

FC Barcelona kicked off their European campaign in emphatic fashion with a 5-1 win over Feyenoord . Lamine Yamal , wearing the captain's armband for the first time, led the way alongside Raphinha on a dream night for Hansi Flick's side.

The downside for the Spanish teams was experienced by Atlético de Madrid . Despite taking the lead at Anfield through Marcos Llorente from a Julián Álvarez assist, the Rojiblancos could not withstand Liverpool 's pressure and ended up losing 2-1 after goals from Szoboszlai and Mac Allister .

Rodri Hernández has sought to draw a line under the controversy sparked by his recent comments about Valencia CF . The Spain international midfielder publicly apologized, insisting that he never meant any disrespect toward the club or its supporters, and also revealed that he had already contacted Valencia captain José Luis Gayà privately.

Ferran shines for PSG and Arsenal get the job done

Elsewhere in the European matchday, Paris Saint-Germain put on a scoring masterclass with a 6-1 thrashing of Slovan Bratislava , featuring a hat-trick from Ferran Torres and a brace from Ousmane Dembélé . Meanwhile, Arsenal showed their experience to take three crucial points at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona by beating Napoli 0-1 thanks to a goal from Martin Ødegaard .

The day's biggest bombshell is happening in the offices. Lionel Messi is on the verge of completing the purchase of CD Eldense . The deal between the Argentine legend and the club from Alicante is completely agreed, with only the official signature missing to confirm his arrival in the boardroom.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany’s Champions League ambition well received by Bayern Munich’s top brass
articles.summary: FC Bayern’s bosses are loving Kompany’s UCL ambitions.
articles.body:
They came close to a treble last season, but the only step forward for Bayern Munich this season from last season would be winning the Champions League. In one of the competitions most exciting two-legged ties, Bayern narrowly missed out on getting to the final in Budapest by losing to eventual winners Paris Saint-Germain in the semifinals 6-5 on aggregate, with the first leg in Paris having finished 5-4 in favor of PSG. There were some questionable calls in the second leg at the Allianz Arena, but the football on display from both sides over two legs fit the billing of what could've been the final at the Puskas Arena in Budapest, but Bayern had to settle with the domestic double.

This time around, Vincent Kompany is hungry for the Champions League. Bayern set scoring records on their way to winning the Bundesliga last season as well as the DFB-Pokal, but the Belgian manager is far less concerned with records than he is with silverware.

Per information from Bild's Julian Agardi and Michael Schröer (via @iMiaSanMia ), Kompany had publicly reiterated to his squad during their preseason tour in Asia his bold desire and ambition to win this season's Champions League. The Bundesliga and Pokal are still priorities, but he wants the European Cup.

This public affirmation to the squad during preseason went down particularly well in the eyes of Bayern's hierarchy. The club's front office, supervisory board, and executive board very much like the fact that Kompany had made his ambitions felt clear so early on, especially after the club had done well to get their transfer business done early in bringing in Nathaniel Brown from Eintracht Frankfurt and Ismael Saibari from PSV Eindhoven. In addition to players, there's also been more established consistency and continuity amongst the club's front office with Max Eberl, Christoph Freund and Jan-Christian Dreesen all getting contract extensions after the recent supervisory board meeting took place. The harmonious balance at the club right now is something to be cherished.

In his third year as Bayern manager, winning the Champions League would be the icing on the cake for Kompany. Regardless, the club knows what they have with him – a manager who states his intentions clearly, is an excellent man manager, protects his players, and delivers with results on the pitch; a true embodiment of the Mia San Mia mindset.

articles.title: Iker Casillas takes a swipe at Real Madrid defence with Thibaut Courtois joke: ‘A bad sign’
articles.summary: Real Madrid legend Iker Casillas offered a typically candid assessment of the club while attending the launch of the 55th edition of the Panini LaLiga sticke...
articles.body:
Real Madrid legend Iker Casillas offered a typically candid assessment of the club while attending the launch of the 55th edition of the Panini LaLiga sticker album, with Thibaut Courtois and Jose Mourinho both providing memorable moments.

Casillas was asked to name the leading candidates for the best player of the 2025/26 season.

The former Spain and Real Madrid goalkeeper initially focused on the attacking stars before being reminded that goalkeepers were also eligible.

"I think Lamine, Mbappe , Vinicius and Raphinha could be in it," the former footballer admitted.

Casillas made a joke about Courtois in a humorous way. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

"What about Courtois?" asked the event's presenter, journalist Felipe del Campo, to which he said, "Ah, goalkeepers too? In that case, yes," replied Iker.

That gave Casillas the opening to make a joke at Real Madrid's expense, using Courtois' status as one of the club's most important players to poke fun at their defensive performances.

"It's fine to have Courtois in the top three. But if the goalkeeper is the best player in the team, that's a bad sign," he remarked with a laugh.

Casillas gives blunt Mourinho description

The afternoon produced another notable moment when Casillas was handed a Jose Mourinho trading card and asked to describe the Portuguese manager in one word.

Casillas and Mourinho had a turbulent relationship. (Photo by Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images)

Their time together at Real Madrid was famously complicated, making the question particularly interesting.

Casillas, however, did not offer a conventional one-word answer.

"More intense and a harder worker than these two," was all he said, pointing to Alvaro García of Rayo Vallecano and Johan Mojica of Getafe , who were standing next to him and had previously described each other in that way.

The response was brief but unmistakably humorous, allowing Casillas to acknowledge Mourinho's intense personality without turning the moment into a serious discussion about their past relationship.

articles.title: Barcelona ace Rodri apologises to Valencia after controversial comments at Mestalla: ‘Hope they return to where they belong’
articles.summary: Barcelona midfielder Rodri has apologised to Valencia after his comments from the Mestalla bench were caught on camera during Barça’s 5-0 victory last weeken...
articles.body:
Barcelona midfielder Rodri has apologised to Valencia after his comments from the Mestalla bench were caught on camera during Barça 's 5-0 victory last weekend.

Rodri was substituted in the 62nd minute with Barcelona already three goals ahead, but the midfielder remained involved in the action from the bench.

Sitting beside Pau Cubarsi , he discussed Valencia's performance with his teammate while watching the remainder of the match.

His comments were picked up by the cameras, with Rodri speaking openly without covering his mouth.

After Barcelona's 5-1 Champions League victory over Feyenoord, Rodri specifically asked to address the incident and offered an apology to those who felt offended.

"I want to apologise to everyone who may have felt offended by my words, both players and fans.

Rodri made some controversial comments during Valencia win. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

"I've already spoken with my friend Gaya to apologise. It was a reaction of surprise; I hope Valencia can return to where it belongs," he said, as per Mundo Deportivo .

The incident occurred during Rodri's first La Liga start for Barcelona since returning to Spain.

With the midfielder substituted after 62 minutes, he took a place on the Mestalla bench alongside Cubarsi.

As Barcelona continued to dominate, Rodri reacted to what he was seeing and questioned Valencia's level of performance.

"They're really weak—these guys are really weak… Really weak. They're really bad, man. They're terrible.

"How did they finish last season? They didn't even make it past midfield in the second half…," Rodri told Cubarsi at different points .

Rodri has publicly apologised to Valencia. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

The remarks were made privately to a teammate but were captured clearly by the television cameras, turning an off-the-cuff reaction into a public talking point.

Rodri's apology now appears to be an attempt to draw a line under the episode, particularly after he acknowledged the potential impact his words could have had on Valencia players and supporters.

Rodri's decision to apologise was the sensible response once his private comments became public.

Footballers regularly react emotionally during matches, but television cameras can turn conversations intended only for teammates into public statements.

The midfielder did not attempt to deny what he said. Instead, he acknowledged that his words could have caused offence and apologised to Valencia players and supporters.

The home side in the Friday primetime match is 1. FC Union Berlin (0-1-1, 15th), who managed to come back from 1-3 down against Eintracht Frankfurt for a 3-3 draw in their opening match - but are returning home after an 0-4 defeat to Bayer 04 Leverkusen last weekend.

Despite difficult challenges to begin the season, Mauro Lustrinelli's side have the fourth-best shots to shot on target rate in the Bundesliga, with 10 shots on target from 24 attempts (41,7%) - ahead of the likes of FC Bayern München , RB Leipzig , VfB Stuttgart , Eintracht Frankfurt, Borussia Dortmund , and even their opposition this weekend, FC Schalke 04, who managed 6 shots on target from 15 attempts (40,0%).

Union and Schalke have played six matches since the former promoted to the Bundesliga for the first time in the 2019/20 season. Their head-to-head record is 1-4-1, but it is worth noting that Schalke's win (2-1) came in 2019/20; the most recent season head-to-head record in 2022/23 saw the match in Berlin finish scoreless, but the match in Gelsenkirchen finish 6-1 to Union, on goals from Sheraldo Becker (twice), Sven Michel (twice), Morten Thorsby , and Janik Haberer .

1. FC Union Berlin has six injuries to report, five of which are expected to heal within the next two weeks. Serbian striker Andrej Ilić (illness) is the first name that will likely return to training, expected to recover in the next week. German centre-back Marvin Friedrich (unknown), French centre-back Stanley N'Soki (calf), Swiss winger Kastriot Imeri (thigh), and Scottish striker Oliver Burke (Achilles tendon) are all expected to return in mid-to-late September.

The only long-term injury is to German defender Andrik Markgraf (cruciate ligament), who will be unable to play for the club until March 2027 at the earliest.

On the other side of the field is FC Schalke 04 (0-1-1, 14th), who are coming off a surprising 0-0 draw with FC Bayern München and also have one point through two matches - with a +1 better goal differential at -3 (0-3), despite having failed to score on their six shots on target. Schalke are one of only three Bundesliga teams that have failed to register a goal through their first two matches, with the other two being another newly-promoted side in SC Paderborn 07 as well as Hamburger SV .

Miron Muslić played a conservative mode of defending in the match against Bayern, more centralised and without taking extreme risks close to the box - and it seemed to work well, as the Gelsenkirchen club managed just five fouls compared to twelve from Bayern. Two matches into the season, Schalke have committed the least fouls of any club in the Bundesliga (11), twelve less than Union Berlin (23) and twenty-two less than the team with the most, Hamburger SV (33).

Goalkeeping will also be a major factor in this match, with 33-year-old Loris Karius being a standout player with the Nordrhein-Westfalen club since his arrival in 2024/25. The Biberach, Baden-Württemberg-born keeper currently holds the league lead for saves per match, with 7,5, and his 83,3% save percentage is fourth-best. It is also worth noting that Karius' last Bundesliga season prior to this campaign was as a member of 1. FC Union Berlin, being loaned from Liverpool FC for four matches in the 2020/21 season.

FC Schalke 04 have a slightly shorter list of absences, with only three injuries and a suspension. Swiss right-back Adrian Gantenbein (ankle) is set to return in mid-to-late September, along with French forward Bryan Lasme (calf); Turkish midfielder Ayman Gülasi (unknown), who has since been moved down to the second team, will be unable to return until the end of the year.

German defensive midfielder Ron Schallenberg will not play in this match due to a two-match ban from the DFB Sports Tribunal, having picked up a red card for a tackle on FC Augsburg 's Michael Gregoritsch in the sixty-second minute of their first match at WWK Arena.
