articles.title: Courtois no cambia pese a los cambios: 100 partidos y otro milagro bajo la mirada de Nuno Santos
articles.standfirst: El belga celebró su centenar en Champions con otra exhibición ante el Inter y siete paradas decisivas
articles.summary: El belga celebró su centenar en Champions con otra exhibición ante el Inter y siete paradas decisivas
articles.body: Hay cosas que cambian en el Real Madrid y otras que siempre resisten al paso del tiempo. Cambian los entrenadores, los métodos de trabajo y los compañeros. Pero lo que no cambia es Thibaut Courtois. Cuando el Madrid necesita un milagro, siempre aparece el belga. Ante el Inter se repitió la historia. El belga firmó otra de esas noches que le confirman como el mejor portero del mundo. Siete paradas, varias de enorme dificultad, para sostener a un Madrid que durante muchos minutos estuvo sometido por el conjunto italiano. Courtois apareció desde el principio y fue decisivo hasta el final, cuando el partido entró en combustión en los minutos finales con el 2-1. Otro partido del Madrid ganado desde la portería. Hasta Mourinho lo dejó claro después del encuentro. Para el técnico portugués, el MVP debía haber sido Courtois. Una declaración que explica mejor la importancia que sigue teniendo el belga en este Real Madrid. La noche ante el Inter tenía además un significado especial. Courtois disputó su partido número 100 en la Champions y entró en uno de los clubes más selectos de la competición. El reparto de su centenar tiene, obviamente, predominio blanco: 72 encuentros con el Real Madrid, 16 con el Chelsea y 12 con el Atlético. Courtois es el primer futbolista belga que alcanza los 100 partidos en Champions y el octavo portero que consigue semejante cifra. Y el centenario llegó con otra exhibición. Courtois ya pertenece a la historia de una competición que le regaló probablemente la noche más importante de su carrera. La final de París de 2022 ante el Liverpool es una de las mayores actuaciones de un portero en una final de la Champions. Entonces realizó nueve paradas y fue elegido mejor jugador del partido. Cuatro años después, su capacidad para decidir encuentros permanece intacta. Esta temporada, sin embargo, presentaba un cambio importante para Courtois. La llegada de Jose Mourinho supuso también una transformación en su equipo de trabajo y la salida de Luis Llopis, con quien Courtois había construido durante años una relación extraordinariamente estrecha. Llopis había trabajado mano a mano con el belga durante ocho años y se había convertido en una figura fundamental en su día a día. Pero Mourinho llegó al Real Madrid con su propio preparador de porteros, Nuno Santos, hombre de absoluta confianza del portugués, y el club decidió apostar por el nuevo equipo técnico. Courtois, siempre agradecido a Llopis, entendió y aceptó la decisión. Asumió que se trataba de una decisión del club y se puso inmediatamente a trabajar con Santos y sus nuevos métodos. Para un portero, cambiar de preparador después de tantos años no era una cuestión menor, pero la respuesta de Tibu ha sido sobresaliente. Sigue transmitiendo la misma seguridad, conserva intactos los reflejos y mantiene esa capacidad para hacerse enorme cuando el delantero tiene toda la portería delante. Courtois es uno de los líderes del Real Madrid. Por edad, trayectoria, rendimiento y personalidad, su voz tiene peso dentro del vestuario. Ha vivido prácticamente de todo de blanco: momentos complicados, Champions, remontadas, noches históricas y también la grave lesión de rodilla que amenazó con apartarle durante mucho tiempo de su mejor nivel. Regresó de ella siendo el mismo. Ese recorrido explica también la decisión que acaba de adoptar respecto a Bélgica. Courtois ha decidido no disputar la Nations League con su selección, porque considera que necesita administrar mejor sus esfuerzos. Su intención es aprovechar esas ventanas internacionales para descansar, trabajar y reducir riesgos después de haber sufrido diferentes problemas físicos durante las últimas temporadas. Tras darlo siempre todo con Bélgica, su prioridad inmediata está clara ahora: el Real Madrid. Courtois quiere alargar su carrera al máximo nivel y entiende que para conseguirlo necesita escuchar cada vez más a su cuerpo. Tiene 34 años y conoce perfectamente las exigencias de una temporada en el Real Madrid, donde prácticamente cada partido obliga a competir al límite. Porque Courtois tiene una obsesión para esta temporada: volver a ganar. El belga quiere dejar atrás la sequía de títulos del último curso y volver a levantar trofeos con el Real Madrid. Sabe que el equipo está iniciando una nueva etapa con Mourinho y que todavía tiene mucho camino por recorrer, pero también que su papel será fundamental mientras el nuevo proyecto termina de asentarse. Y él ya ha empezado a poner de su parte con exhibiciones como la del Inter.

articles.title: Ballon d’Or 2026 power rankings: Who leads the race after nominees announced?
articles.summary: Here’s how the top 10 contenders rank in the race to lift the Ballon d’Or in October
articles.body:
The race for the Ballon d'Or is entering its final stretch with the 30-name shortlist for the men's award now confirmed following the 2026 World Cup .

Spain's triumph over Argentina in the final will surely bode well for the likes of 2024 winner Rodri and Lamine Yamal in their pursuit of the individual accolade, who will look to start the new club season with some spellbinding performances to complement their part in winning football's most coveted trophy.

Harry Kane remains the favourite for the Ballon d'Or, however, following his sublime goalscoring campaign with Bayern Munich and after making a series of important inverventions at the World Cup with England, too – can he replicate that unparalleled form in the early months of 2026/27 to make team achievements irrelevant come October's ceremony?

During the World Cup eight-time Ballon d'Or winner Lionel Messi showed that he can still force himself into the conversation at the age of 39, firing eight goals to propel Argentina to the final and briefly take the crown as the competition's all-time top goalscorer - until he was eclipsed by Kylian Mbappe .

Here's how the top 10 front-runners stack up in The Independent's Ballon d'Or 2026 power rankings:

Vinicius squeezes into our Ballon d'Or power rankings, mainly to spare myself some angry emails from those affiliated to Real Madrid and Brazil. I joke, kind of.

The 2024 runner-up had another strong season at the Bernabeu, netting 22 goals in 36 appearances, though like Mbappe was unable to inspire the club to a trophy.

Similar could be said about his World Cup; he was one of the few bright lights in a wooden Brazil side under Carlo Ancelotti, which eventually succumbed to Norway and Erling Haaland .

A much-discussed move to Arsenal during the summer did not materialise, so the 26-year-old needs some form at Real Madrid to spark life into his Ballon d'Or bid.

Crystal Palace could only keep him in Croydon for so long.

With Bayern Munich and France, Olise has established himself as one of the world's best attackers, a talent so bright that the German giants did well to ward off interest from the likes of Real Madrid - who no doubt saw the World Cup partnership he formed with Mbappe and want to reunite the pair in the Spanish capital at some stage.

Will his electrifying performances be enough to win the Ballon d'Or? Probably not, this year. But he's in the conversation, which is a statement in itself.

For unrivalled football insight from Miguel Delaney, join Inside Football here .

How was this man's place on the England plane ever in question?! Thomas Tuchel's player of the tournament, Bellingham served his critics a serious helping of humble pie by guiding the Three Lions to the elusive World Cup bronze.

That beautiful redemption arc , on its own, has Bellingham on this list. That's because the season that preceded the World Cup wasn't spectacular. Injuries limited him to just 13 goal contributions for Real Madrid in another trophyless campaign.

It's why his chances of winning the Ballon d'Or are still low compared to the competition. But as was proved at the World Cup - don't count him out.

Their first World Cup since 1998, Haaland ensured Norway lived up to their dark-horse status by powering them to the last-eight. On the way, his unrelenting goalscoring exploits humbled Brazil , sending the five-time winners packing. Away from the big-hitting nations, Haaland was far and away the tournament's standout player, to little surprise.

Add that to a pretty bog-standard Haaland season for City - just the 38 goals last year, the fourth season he's hit 30+ at the Etihad - which saw him lift a domestic double. Legacy-defining stats for nearly anyone else, but normal service for the big Norwegian.

As prolific as he may be, he's currently a definite outsider in the Ballon d'Or race. That may change if he emulates the start to the season he had last year, which saw him smack home 13 in his first 10 league outings. Recency bias can be a powerful thing...

Had France won the World Cup, as many expected them to do leading up to that drab semi-final exit , Dembele would have been heavily favoured to secure a second successive Ballon d'Or. The combination of World Cup and Champions League winners' medals is a bit of a cheat code.

That would've been quite the gimme for a player who, let's be honest, was France's fourth best attacker at the World Cup. And while, like last year, he ended the season as Paris Saint-Germain 's top scorer with a Ligue 1 and Champions League to boot, he only managed about half of his goalscoring output.

His trophy haul still carries enough weight to be comfortably in the top 10 contenders, but the failure to lift that World Cup title gives him only an outside chance to go back-to-back - and we think that's fair. Sorry Ousmane, but this year shouldn't be your year.

He couldn't again, could he? Messi's inclusion on this list encapsulates the significance of the World Cup in deciding the Ballon d'Or winner; he's not going to take the accolade for his MLS exploits, is he. But fair play to the eight-time winner; at 39, he showed he very much still had it.

Messi's eight goals propelled Argentina to the World Cup final, where they were rightly defeated by Spain - had he lifted back-to-back titles, he'd probably be towards the top two of this list. After all, he claimed the 2023 award after La Albiceleste 's triumph 10 months earlier, by which time he was on the books at Inter Miami .

Even with his runners-up medal, Indy Sport writers had him as the player of the tournament . That, combined with the jury's historic love for the Argentinian, means you can't exactly write him off. Messi's retirement from international football , announced following the death of his father, Jorge, underlines that this is now his final chance to win another Ballon d'Or.

It feels pretty crazy to think that, at 27, Mbappe still doesn't have a Ballon d'Or to his name, given he's been at the top of the game for what feels like forever now.

Once again, he's very much in the mix this time around. His Golden Boot at the World Cup will do most of the heavy lifting, with his 10 goals in North America seeing him pass first Miroslav Klose and then Lionel Messi as the tournament's all-time record goalscorer. Both he and Messi would have felt hard done by not to go home with the Golden Ball.

But lest we forget, despite the toxicity that surrounded his club season with Real Madrid, he didn't exactly experience a drop-off in performance. He bagged 42 goals in 44 games, all while being hounded at the Bernabeu - and while it wasn't enough to prevent another trophyless season for Los Blancos , you can't knock his output.

Mbappe still believes he is the best in the world and if he can get along with Jose Mourinho and get 2026/27 off to a flyer, he could well shoot up to the pinnacle of these rankings.

And back to the World Cup superiority complex we go, sort of. Yamal will surely win his fair share of Ballon d'Ors across his career, but the 19-year-old could very well end up taking home his first this year, going one better than his runners-up finish in 2025.

Yamal became the first player under 20 to appear at both a European Championship final and a World Cup final - he won both. While his output was pretty modest for his standards, he was influential throughout the tournament for Spain - and that's after coming into it carrying a hamstring injury.

He also bagged 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions for Barcelona in another LaLiga-winning season - hardly a mediocre year for the teenager. He's more than in with a shout.

England captain Kane is still the odds-on favourite to win the Ballon d'Or despite failing to set the World Cup alight quite like he managed the Bundesliga in 2025/26. That's a testament to just how prolific he was last term.

Kane was the top goalscorer in Europe, hitting 61 goals in 51 games across all competitions as he spearheaded Bayern towards the league and cup double; he's added silverware to his ever-present individual numbers. He was then hardly irrelevant at the World Cup, scoring six goals - including a crucial late brace against DR Congo to spare his country serious embarrassment - as England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 .

If his club form continues into the new campaign, the jury may have to put their emphasis on the World Cup and wider team achievement to one side. There is also the significance of the location of the Ballon d'Or ceremony to consider; it will be held in London, to commemorate the 70th anniversary of the very first Ballon d'Or won by England's Sir Stanley Matthews. Could Kane become just the fifth Englishman to win the prize?

"Of course, now it is out of my hands, it is down to the voters and the people who decide it," Kane said. "The season I had was my best season by far and we'll have to wait and see."

You might not like it, but the weight of the World Cup in the eyes of the Ballon d'Or jury is undeniable. Just ask Luka Modric .

Rodri had a sensational World Cup at the heart of Spain's midfield, shielding their rock-solid defence while acting as the metronome that took play forward. His influence took him to the Golden Ball ahead of top goalscorers Messi and Mbappe - and we feel like that could be the precursor to him bringing home a second Ballon d'Or in October.

That would feel like a bit of an injustice, considering he didn't have the most spectacular domestic season. Returning from injury with Manchester City , it took him a while to properly find his feet in a campaign that saw Pep Guardiola's side win the FA Cup and League Cup, but miss out on the Premier League title. But the World Cup is the World Cup - and whether you agree with the importance of team achievements in an individual award, the reality is that it does matter a hell of a lot.

Having now made his move to Barcelona and slotted in seamlessly into the base of the Spanish champion's midfield, carrying on his World Cup form in LaLiga and the Champions League could also swing the jury in his favour.

articles.title: Taylor aims to make Wales a force in deaf football
articles.summary: Having transitioned from player to head coach, James Taylor plans to make Wales a force to be reckoned with in deaf football.
articles.body:
Wales and England come face-to-face in Llandarcy on Friday, 11 September, the latest chapter in the rollercoaster story of the Wales Deaf men's football side.

Re-established in 2023, they drew with England and beat both Scotland and Ireland in their first three matches.

However, from such a promising start the Wales Deaf Football Association (WDFA) found themselves going backwards.

In 2024 the squad travelled to Turkey, full of hope for the EuroDeaf Championships but lost all four of their group games.

A review led to a change of the organisation's backroom staff structure and the appointment of a new head coach, former Wales Deaf forward James Taylor.

Despite a 7-1 hammering by England in his first game in charge, Taylor has big plans for Wales - and knows all about dealing with the ups and downs football can throw at you, for 'Jamo' has quite the story himself.

Taylor was an experienced Welsh league player who once aspired to be a professional, but total deafness in his left ear prevented him from reaching his potential.

"It's probably one of the reasons that let me down in the professional world, because anything that was coming to the left-hand side, I didn't hear," Taylor said.

"I started grassroots football for the local team, Afan Lido. I was fortunate to be in a successful team from the age of eight to 16.

"We won everything that was possible for us."

Taylor's goal for the under-16 team against Swansea City caught the eye of Swansea scouts and he later spent two years in the Vetch Field club's youth training scheme.

Taylor's youth team manager at Swansea was retired Wales forward Alan Curtis, who he described as a "legend and a gentleman".

"I grew up in a Swansea sporting household. My father was a massive Swansea City supporter," Taylor recalled.

"I was born in the morning and he was on the North Bank in the afternoon watching the Swans. His idol was Alan Curtis, so that just made my father proud as punch.

"When we went to places like Cheltenham and Bristol, we'd normally stop off and pick up my old man, and you can imagine him in a minibus with Alan Curtis driving - he chewed the ear off him!"

Taylor made a single senior appearance for Swansea, against Haverfordwest in the West Wales Senior Cup in the 1997-98 season.

But a serious ankle injury thwarted his second season and he was subsequently told he would not be taken on as a professional.

"They did reassure me that if I went to any team and carried on scoring goals, they'd put me back in and keep looking at me, but unfortunately, those goals died away," said Taylor.

He returned to Afan Lido before stints at Port Talbot, Neath and Goytre. Then at the age of 43, Taylor won the first of three caps for Wales Deaf men's team.

In February 2026 Taylor took charge of his first match, facing England at the FA's training headquarters, St George's Park.

But Wales' visit proved a sharp lesson, with that 7-1 defeat.

"It hurt, and I believe it hurts harder as a manager. However, it provided a valuable benchmark for where we are as a squad," Taylor said.

As part of the re-building process, a talent identification day was held at Dragon Park in Newport in June, which saw more than 20 new players attend.

"It was a real success with a great turnout. There are a few new faces coming in, as well as a couple of familiar faces from old returning," he added.

"The standard of football was good, the players took on board the information really well, and their attitudes and commitment were excellent."

Wales - like England - are hoping to send a squad to compete in the inaugural Deaf International Football Association Deaf Football World Cup in Australia in November 2027, and then six months later to the 2028 European Deaf Football Championships in Italy .

So, for Taylor, their schedule leading up to the tournaments needs to be filled with as many matches as possible.

"We're not going to be going camp, camp, camp... it's only in a game when you can really see the development in the boys and the squad," he said.

They recently played a friendly against Newport Corinthians, who play in the third tier of the Welsh pyramid, losing 6-4.

"The thing that stood out for us against them was that our boys haven't had those minutes in their legs, where Newport Corries I'm sure have had a good pre-season," said Taylor.

He also knows the international against England in Llandarcy on Friday (19:30 BST) will be another big step up.

"We need to start making waves and noises," he said.

"I haven't taken on this management role just to post a load on social media. My hopes are to make Wales a force in deaf football.

"I'm only interested in the players who are 100% committed to Wales now.

"I'm not saying they haven't in the past, but maybe seeing a bit more competition coming into camp will give them that push, not only for Wales, but in their personal football journeys as well.

"That's all I ever want to do is make the players the best version of themselves on a football pitch."

articles.title: 💰 Squad values, Como top Italy's giants by +€150m 🤯! But Real, monstrous🚀
articles.summary: It’s time to take stock after a summer transfer window that reshaped the landscape of world football. The first two days of the Champions League have already...
articles.body:
It's time to take stock after a summer transfer window that reshaped the landscape of world football. The first two days of the Champions League have already given us some verdicts, unfortunately negative ones for the Italian sides. Both Inter and Napoli , in fact, lost on their respective debuts, albeit against two giants like Real and Arsenal .

Inter, above all, have plenty of regrets, given the mistakes that led to the two blancos goals, also taking into account the "transfer market" factor, which in the club's plans was supposed to bring the Italian champions closer to Europe's elite .

Curtis Jones , Stones and Spence — although the latter is actually still sidelined — were all signings made with the idea of adding dynamism to the squad, to bring them closer to the level of the other top sides. But Inter, of course, are not the only ones to have changed...

In the Top 50 clubs by squad value, Serie A has eight teams , a result that is far from negative compared with the other European leagues. The comparison with the Premier League, however, remains merciless : the ranking features no fewer than 19 English clubs out of 20 , with only Hull City missing from the list, while West Ham also appear, the only Championship side included.

Outside Europe's five major leagues, the team with the most valuable squad is Porto , ahead of Galatasaray . To find the first club outside the UEFA area, you have to go all the way down to Al-Hilal in 57th, while Flamengo, in 62nd place, lead the South American contingent.

At the top of the standings remain Real Madrid , who after the Mourinho-style revolution have managed to hold on to first place. The arrivals of Diomande, Dumfries, Konaté and other top-level players have allowed the Merengues to fend off the challenge of Manchester City , the protagonists of what has been described as the richest transfer window ever, and PSG , two-time European champions. Just off the podium, meanwhile, are Arsenal, who will once again try to chase the dream of the treble .

Real Madrid themselves are the clearest example of what the transfer market can deliver: between June and September, Florentino Perez increased the squad's value by around €240 million . Major growth also came for newly promoted sides Hull and Ipswich , at +157 and +120 million respectively, while Como sit between the two English teams and are the Italian club with the biggest increase in value .

In just twelve months, the club from Como has gone from 52nd to 21st place, managing to overtake Roma, Milan and Napoli as well and break firmly into the Top 30.

Naturally, there are also negative signs. The clearest case is Marseille , who are dealing with a particularly difficult moment and an overall estimated loss of around €181 million in squad value. Among the teams hit hardest are also other French clubs, such as Strasbourg and Lyon . Italy , meanwhile, has only two clubs among those in decline, Bologna and Cagliari , with drops that are decidedly more limited.

articles.title: Ronald Araujo speaks out after impressing with backheel assist for Liverpool
articles.summary: The defender’s move is going well.
articles.body:
Ronald Araujo is enjoying life at Liverpool after making the move from Barcelona in the summer transfer window on a season-long loan.

The Uruguayan certainly caught the eye on Wednesday night in the Champions League with a backheel assist in a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid at Anfield.

Araujo spoke to reporters after the game and admitted he is happy playing for Andoni Iraola 's side.

"It was a very difficult match. We knew they were going to make it very difficult for us. We were compact and played our style of football, and we were able to get the three points," he said. "It was a nice shot, a good opportunity inside the box. I was lucky it went between the center backs. I'm very happy and very pleased to be able to help the team. "It's a big team like Barça . You have to give your best and there are high expectations. I'm happy and working hard. I'm eager to give my all and be myself."

articles.standfirst: Los cinco partidos en 18 días han llevado al técnico de Nueva Jersey a utilizar los 22 futbolistas disponibles de su vestuario más otros dos del Sanse, y 18 han sido titulares
articles.summary: Los cinco partidos en 18 días han llevado al técnico de Nueva Jersey a utilizar los 22 futbolistas disponibles de su vestuario más otros dos del Sanse, y 18 han sido titulares
articles.body: Pellegrino Matarazzo ha utilizado en sólo cinco partidos a 24 futbolistas distintos, los 22 que tiene disponibles en su plantilla, en la que Álvaro Odriozola y Pablo Marín son bajas por lesión, y a dos del Sanse, Luken Beitia y Álex Marchal, y hasta 18 de ellos han sido titulares, con lo que parece que el técnico de la Real Sociedad va a tirar más que nunca de las rotaciones, en esta temporada con cuatro competiciones. Matarazzo, que tuvo una pretemporada complicada por las bajas por los internacionales y las lesiones, lo que le llevó a echar mano de hasta 12 futbolistas del segundo equipo, alineó de inicio en el estreno en La Cartuja a Remiro, Aramburu, Jon Martín, Zubeldia, Sergio Gómez, Soler, Herrera, Kubo, Sucic, Barrenetxea y Óskarsson, con Oyarzabal, Marchal, Aihen, Turrientes y Zakharyan entrando desde el banquillo. Las presencias de Ochieng y sobre todo el jugador del Sanse Luken Beitia fueron las grandes sorpresas en su alineación inicial en el Santiago Bernabéu, en donde Gonçalo Guedes tuvo también sus primeros minutos, saliendo desde el banquillo. Jon Gorrotxategi, de baja durante todo el verano, pudo jugar ya en la tercera jornada, la de la primera victoria del curso, 2-1 frente al Espanyol, y después de que en la cuarta, en el empate a cero ante el Celta, no se produjeran novedades, en la quinta en Elche llegaron hasta cuatro: Unai Marrero y Mamadou Sarr, en el once, y Héctor Fort y Jon Pacheco saliendo desde el banquillo. Eran cinco partidos seguidos en sólo 18 días, casi por tanto uno en cada tres, lo que ha llevado a Matarazzo a tirar ya de todos sus futbolistas disponibles y hasta de dos del Sanse, pese a lo que hay unos cuantos que han hecho pleno y han participado en todas las citas, entre ellos Aramburu, Sergio Gómez o el mismísimo Mikel Oyarzabal, que quizás hayan tenido más minutos de los que deberían recién iniciada esta temporada tan cargada.

articles.title: Terry and Sieb shine as LAFC dominate New York Red Bulls to end winless run
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES -- For the first time in weeks, LAFC did not have to spend the final minutes wondering how another lead was going to disappear.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- For the first time in weeks, LAFC did not have to spend the final minutes wondering how another lead was going to disappear.

That alone made Wednesday night feel different.

After watching leads slip away in Salt Lake and enduring three consecutive MLS draws, LAFC finally closed one out, defeating the New York Red Bulls 2-0 at BMO Stadium. The result snapped a six-game league winless streak and gave the Black & Gold their 13th clean sheet of the season, setting a new club record.

More importantly, it showed the kind of defensive response Marc Dos Santos had been looking for.

New York came into the match wanting to combine through the middle and use quick one-twos to work its way into the box. LAFC's defense largely took that option away, limiting the Red Bulls to eight shots and just one on target.

"We defended that part of the box so well," Dos Santos said.

The shutout was particularly meaningful after Saturday's 2-2 draw with Real Salt Lake , when LAFC surrendered another lead and watched two points disappear. Dos Santos admitted that result had lingered with the group, saying there was a "fear of losing" late against New York that caused his team to defend a little deeper than he wanted.

The attack also gave the defense something it had been missing: an early cushion.

Jude Terry opened the scoring in the 21st minute, following up Son Heung-Min 's saved shot and calmly finishing from the edge of the area for his first goal at BMO Stadium. For a 17-year-old who has spent much of the season learning how to make the most of limited opportunities, it was another reminder of the attacking ability Dos Santos sees in him.

Terry has now scored twice this season, but Dos Santos believes the next stage of his development will come on the other side of the ball.

"When he has to track back, when he has to do defensive plays, when he has to win duels, that's the next step for Jude if he wants to become more complete," Dos Santos said.

Terry said the coaching staff has already made that development a priority.

"I'll just keep going," he said. "That'll eventually help me as a player and help the team."

LAFC had chances to put the match away much earlier. Son finished with eight shots, tying his career high in MLS, and Dos Santos felt his team could have gone into halftime with a two- or three-goal advantage.

Instead, the second goal did not arrive until stoppage time.

This time, it came from a player who is still figuring out his place in the team.

Armindo Sieb , making his home debut after entering as a substitute in his second appearance for LAFC, received a pass from Ryan Hollingshead at the top of the box and fired a left-footed shot past a frozen Ethan Horvath . It was Sieb's first MLS goal and another glimpse of what Dos Santos hopes his squad can become once more of its injured players return.

Igor Jesus entered alongside him in the 60th minute, making his first appearance in more than a year after recovering from a knee injury.

For Jesus, simply getting back onto the field carried more weight than the result.

"It was a very challenging year," Jesus said. "There's nothing better than being home today, coming back and getting three points."

Dos Santos immediately noticed the difference. He said LAFC's possession improved when Jesus entered and described the midfielder at his best as one of the league's top three players at his position.

The coach knows he cannot rush that process. More players are expected to return, but until then, LAFC has to keep finding ways to collect points with the group available.

"Until there, we have to scratch, to fight together, and get the most results we can," Dos Santos said.

LAFC remains third in the Western Conference at 40 points, and the club now has three consecutive road matches ahead. After spending much of the past month watching opportunities slip away, the team finally has a result it can build on.

For Terry and Sieb, the night offered another glimpse of LAFC's future. For Jesus, it marked the beginning of a return that could change the team's ceiling.

And for a defense that had spent the previous match surrendering another winnable game, 90 minutes without conceding may have been the most important development of all.

articles.title: El impacto inmediato de Troy Parrott
articles.standfirst: Goles para ganar ante el Real Madrid y en la Champions y enorme seguimiento mediático
articles.summary: Goles para ganar ante el Real Madrid y en la Champions y enorme seguimiento mediático
articles.body: Troy Parrott ha necesitado apenas cuatro partidos para convertirse en uno de los grandes protagonistas del Betis. El delantero irlandés, por el que el club pagó al AZ Alkmaar 16 millones de euros más cuatro en variables por objetivos, está respondiendo a la apuesta del club con dos goles decisivos: el de la victoria ante el Real Madrid en La Cartuja y el 2-3 que culminó el martes la remontada frente al Lille en la Champions. Pero su impacto, sin embargo, va mucho más allá de los tantos. Parrott ha aportado al ataque de Pellegrini un perfil diferente al del Cucho Hernández que mezcla potencia física, capacidad para atacar los espacios y amenazar la espalda de los defensas, recursos para finalizar con las dos piernas y de cabeza... y una facilidad enorme para ganar duelos. Un delantero a la vieja usanza con la portería entre ceja y ceja y cuyos movimientos aportan soluciones de todo tipo a su equipo, tanto en el ataque posicional como en las transiciones. La explosión del irlandés, además, está teniendo una espectacular repercusión en su país y en el Reino Unido, donde comenzó su carrera en el Tottenham. Comentaristas y exfutbolistas analizan en programas de TV de máxima audiencia en las islas la irrupción del goleador en España, se preguntan por qué no triunfó durante su etapa en Londres y apuntan a que, si mantiene esta progresión, podría convertirse a corto plazo incluso en un objetivo para clubes de la Premier League. El Betis ya está recibiendo numerosas peticiones de prestigiosos medios británicos y de habla inglesa interesados en realizar entrevistas y reportajes de todo tipo con el goleador. El plan de comunicación soñado por el club cuando se fijó en Parrott y, confiando ciegamente en que su apuesta era ganadora, decidió protegerse con una cláusula de 100 millones, desvelada por El Desmarque, con la que tener el control del jugador si terminan llegando cantos de sirena desde Inglaterra. En su adaptación a Sevilla está desempeñando un papel importante Héctor Bellerín. El lateral catalán, que habla inglés fluido de sus años en el Arsenal y conoce a la perfección los entresijos y características esenciales del fútbol británico y sus jugadores, se ha convertido en su particular cicerone y en uno de los compañeros que más lo arropan dentro del vestuario. Eso sí, Troy no ha tardado en ganarse el cariño y la admiración de todo el equipo, como demuestran los numerosos comentarios que recibe del planten en sus publicaciones en redes. En Parrott el Betis ha encontrado, más allá del futbolista, a una persona muy familiar y con los pies en el suelo. Llegó a Sevilla acompañado por su madre, sus hermanos y hermanas y por su novia, Lauren Bowry. Ella y uno de sus hermanos viajaron por su cuenta a Lille esta semana, donde mezclados con otros aficionados béticos, pudieron disfrutar en directo del gol de Troy y de una victoria inolvidable en el regreso del Betis a la máxima competición europea tras más de 20 años. Entre quienes observan de cerca su evolución se encuentra Robbie Keane. El histórico delantero, máximo goleador histórico de la selección de la República de Irlanda, mantiene un cariño especial por Parrott y se ha interesado recientemente por cómo le están yendo las cosas en el Betis. Su seguimiento es otra muestra de la expectación que genera en su país un futbolista al que se considera una de las grandes referencias ofensivas de su generación. El interés de Keane tampoco es casual. Conoce a Parrott desde que era un adolescente en la cantera del Tottenham y fue uno de sus primeros referentes. En 2019, cuando formaba parte del cuerpo técnico de la selección irlandesa, llegó a visitarlo en Londres para conocer de cerca su situación y su personalidad. Y desde entonces, ha seguido su evolución, manteniendo el vínculo y aportándole los consejos de quien lo ha vivido todo en el mundo del fútbol. Parrott ha encontrado en Sevilla un escenario ideal para seguir creciendo. Tiene competencia, exigencia y un equipo que aspira a competir en LaLiga y en la Champions; pero también un entrenador que ya le ha dado protagonismo en partidos de máxima importancia. En cuatro encuentros ha pasado de lamentar ocasiones falladas ante Valencia y Levante a ser decisivo frente al Real Madrid y Lille. El camino es largo y su rendimiento deberá sostenerse en el tiempo, pero el Betis ya está comprobando el impacto y la dimensión que puede darle Parrott y el enorme foco internacional que ha abierto con su fichaje.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino: Ex-Tottenham and Chelsea boss hopes to return to Premier League in future
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino speaks to Sky Sports News' Gail Davis in an exclusive interview; ex-Tottenham and Chelsea boss reveals hope of returning to Premier League in future; last month, the Argentine signed a new four-year deal to continue as the manager of the USA men's team
articles.body:
The former Tottenham boss guided the USA team to the last 16 of the World Cup, where the host nation's dreams of victory came to a crashing halt against Belgium, but that barely tells the story of an extraordinary few weeks for the Argentine.

There was Donald Trump - there was always going to be - and the changing-room team talk. There was Trump, FIFA and Folarin Balogun's suspension of his suspension, and along the way, Pochettino became something of a fashion icon.

Then a few weeks later, another significant headline - Pochettino had, a little surprisingly perhaps, signed for four more years with the USA.

Where to start? I smile before jesting, and Pochettino just laughs and says he's ready. His reflections on the World Cup seem like as good a place to get going.

For Pochettino, the biggest takeaway is how much he and his coaching staff, including his long-term lieutenant Jesus Perez, have learned.

"We are much better coaches now," he insists. It is revealing because the World Cup has reinforced his appetite to keep learning and evolving. He talks about the importance of the smallest details, the difficulty of getting every decision right and the challenge of translating his ideas to a group of players who spend far less time together than a club side. He adds, "Everything needs to be perfect."

There were times during the tournament when life must have felt a little wild, I suggest. There's managing at the World Cup, then there's managing at a home World Cup for a nation whose President rather enjoys the spotlight. Unsurprisingly, Pochettino chooses his words carefully, focusing on the support and backing Trump gave the side.

At the time, he was asked about his role in getting the Balogun suspension suspended, and he admitted the "politics and manipulation" did overshadow the game against Belgium. Pochettino understood the anger around the situation, but his role was much simpler - "If you pay attention to the noise, you become crazy." FIFA allowed Balogun to play and he says, "When the letter arrived the day before the game confirming Balogun was available, the decision was straightforward."

Balogun has been in the headlines again over the past few weeks after his proposed move from Monaco to Everton collapsed late on Deadline Day. Pochettino has not spoken to him yet. He has deliberately given him some space because he knows it would have been a difficult situation. He would, he says, have liked to see Balogun playing in the Premier League. Instead, he remains at Monaco, and Pochettino hopes he can get himself into a good place.

'I hope to return to Premier League in future'

There was of course the fashion too. Pochettino has always taken his style seriously, but I am not sure even he could have imagined the impact his touchline navy ensemble would have had. It created its own headlines - not least because Wayne Rooney went out and bought it. "I saw him. He looked good on him, like a top coach," he laughs.

Then, as the footballing world moved on from the World Cup, the rumours linking Pochettino to a number of clubs looking for a manager began. But that speculation was short-lived with the news that he was staying with the USA.

If Pochettino sees out his contract until 2030, six years away from club football feels a long time. Is that his Premier League story over? He disagrees, and for him his desire is not only to be back in English football, but to compete for honours.

"I have the ambition," he says. "My dream now is to be in the USA for four years, but after that, why not? We are still young, and I think coming back is always my goal; to win the Premier League, to be in the Premier League and to build a project with the possibility of winning."

"I love the football here. I think to have the chance again is one of my wishes and I hope that happens."

That unfinished business takes me back to an interview I did with Pochettino 18 months or so ago - he spoke about wanting to one day return to Spurs. At the time, Tottenham were struggling under Ange Postecoglou. Since then, Postecoglou has gone, and Thomas Frank and Igor Tudor have arrived and departed as the club got perilously close to the drop.

So did that call to rescue the club ever come? Pochettino says of a return: "Always I say, one day, why not?"

So was it ever a possibility this time? Pochettino says: "People talk and maybe we receive some approach, but it never was close." Not this time then.

What about some of those other jobs - at one point AC Milan looked like a possible destination.

"We were not open during the World Cup to talk with different clubs that were interested," he says.

But were there clubs interested? "Yes, always," he says as if that is the norm. "Yes, always have different, you know, options," he teases.

I try again - did any of them come close to taking your attention? "We never gave the opportunity to be close. We always closed the door before it got close."

Poch assesses old clubs Spurs and Chelsea

So what of where his old club Tottenham are right now, because I joke it is never dull at Spurs.

"They are investing like other clubs", and Pochettino sees the logic after a couple of difficult seasons. Tottenham have changed their approach and are spending big on players who already know the Premier League. I think back to how close Pochettino was to delivering Spurs glory in the league and Europe and how little he spent by comparison - what would he have given to have had £300m to spend? There's a mischievous smile, and he pretends he couldn't possibly understand what £300m is.

So does he think this new strategy will work? "You never know," he replies. "We need time to see if that works or not.

"Like in all the games, when you make a decision like a coach that can work well or not. I think it's a different strategy and a different way to operate. I always wish the best for Tottenham because it's in my heart."

There's also been a big shift in direction at his former side Chelsea. The head coach role he held two years ago has now been changed to manager, while there has been a significant change in transfer policy with the club buying Premier League-ready players rather than projects under Xabi Alonso.

Pochettino is reluctant to make direct comparisons, but he sees similarities in the ambition of both clubs, and concedes "buying players like this you can expect to fight, to be a contender for the Premier League."

Chelsea's defeat to Arsenal has already provided an early reality check, but Pochettino is urging patience with Alonso.

"Of course they are disappointed after the defeat against Arsenal, but I think we need to give time to Xabi's first season after three games in the Premier League," he says.

"I think we need to give time, and of course for Tottenham the same."

For Pochettino, Arsenal are very much in pole position.

"Mikel [Arteta] is the best coach in the Premier League today," he says. "Knowing what he needs to do, it's going to be tough to beat them."
